Read this first: P0 is not the clean plant its records describe. Its smooth rule causes full 9 m/s² ALKS braking that every 1-Hz metric misses (V367). So the sawtooth was not removed, and the braking, free-road and sawtooth statements of V324, V327, V329 and baseline v1 do not hold. Flow, delay, collisions, TTC and fuel stand for the plant as built, but every phase 1-3 result ran on it.
Where things stand, 2026-11-05. Plant: P0d is accepted and stored as baseline v2 (V376): hidden braking gone, 6 of 7 check items, undertakes counted as met with a disclosure. The review found a second hidden source under controllers, the V2V headway rise; it and the slowdown taper are fixed for this run (V382). DRL: the shot passed its fixed reading, 7 of 7 clearly ahead of r4a1 (V368), exploratory and on P0. Next: confirmatory 3, revision 3, approved in V383, against 70 rules in 6 forms. Code reviewed, pre-run checks pass. STARTING About 8 hours, units c3-chain and c3-guard, status in /home/catalin/work/phd/v5b1_runs/conf3/status.txt. Nothing here reports its result. If no cell is won, this DRL line closes (V378).

Read first, in this order

  1. The hidden braking and the P0c check: read these before trusting any plant statement.
  2. Rules for the new agent (section 10): discuss before building, per-CAV naming, every decision logged.
  3. Path map (section 2): how the project got here.
  4. 20-cell map, rule check and the shot: the current evidence.
  5. docs/research/protocols/confirmatory_3.md (draft), confirmatory_2.md and docs/research/baseline_v1/BASELINE.md, whose braking numbers V367 corrects.
  6. The last 30 rows of docs/decisions.md, then the decision tree (section 12). Next step is the author's pick.

Names used everywhere

r1m3

1 ramp lane, 3 main lanes. Called m32 in code and old records (V319)

P0

r1m3 with lcAssertive 1.4 and the smooth no-undertaking rule (V328). Recorded as clean, but it hides hard braking (V367)

P0c, P0d

P0c: P0 with the rule's cap eased every 0.1 s (V370). P0d: also an 8-s look-ahead and braking up to 4.4 m/s² when needed. P0d is the accepted plant, baseline v2 (V376)

d0-d6

the trained DRL policies, one per learner: d0-d2 in confirmatory 2, d0-d6 in the shot

r2m3

P0 settings plus a second ramp and acceleration lane 4a (V354)

r1m2

1 ramp lane, 2 main lanes, a transfer check (V330)

ALKS

the automated vehicles the controllers act on, 50 % of the fleet; human cars 42.5 %, trucks 7.5 %

Level

demand in veh/h: 4,090, 4,600, 5,300, 6,000

per-CAV

one shared policy deciding per ALKS. Older files say C, F, G, H, C0-C2; never say C (V309)

p333, a333

digits are headway levels up, merge, down: 0 = 1.6, 1 = 1.2, 2 = 1.0, 3 = 0.8 s. p: each vehicle ramps on its own clock; a: a zone target, one level per 60 s

X1, X2, H1, H2, S

tapered slowdown on edge 4, on edge 3, slow truck, ramp bursts, steady (confirmatory 2)

Sawtooth

an ALKS braking on free road every few seconds under SUMO's no-undertaking logic; in all stored results before V324; on P0 it only changed form, out of the 1-Hz sample (V367)

V1510-13No variable speed limits and no HDV lane limits.
full entry
No variable speed limits and no HDV lane limits. The system is CAV commands only: CAVs keep a steady speed for the circumstances (fewer decelerations and accelerations) and so steady the traffic around them. A deployed system without VSL gantries is cheaper. HDVs are not measured by the system | decided. Ramp meters dropped too (may be added later): CAV commands are the only actuator. Evaluation covers all vehicles: HDVs add non-linearity and realism, and harm to them shows in the total cost
Claude, result or own callSee entryV32 Infrastructure comparators (research question):
V1610-13Headline = a mix of energy, delay and CAV hard braking
full entry
Headline = a mix of energy, delay and CAV hard braking, designed so that energy cannot be won by slowing traffic: the author's earlier harmonisation results cost the CAVs too much speed. The trade-off is designed in from the start | decided: form A, generalised cost (value of time × delay + energy price × kWh + a cost per CAV hard brake, per vehicle-km, over all vehicles); the training reward uses the same mix. Open: the values and their sources, the delay guard x %, the sensitivity rows

V6410-13Road redesign, option 1 (V58):
full entry
Road redesign, option 1 (V58): the lane drop moves to the end. Layout:
• 3 lanes 0–3,000 m (Z1 2,000–3,000);
• merge 1 at 3,000–3,250 (OR1 joins; auxiliary lane continues as X1);
• 3 lanes 3,250–4,500 (Z2 3,500–4,500);
• merge 2 at 4,500–4,750 (OR2 joins; auxiliary lane continues as X2);
• 3 lanes 4,750–6,000 (Z3 5,000–6,000);
• lane drop 3→2 at 6,000;
• 2 lanes 6,000–9,250.

(1) Incident response pays: the per-type plan IP (switch at onset, back at clearance) beats the no-incident controller N by 16–41 % in all 4 cells. (2) Per-incident information adds nothing beyond the per-type plan: cross-fitted ORX vs IP is 0–1 % (lower CIs ≤ 0). (3) The page's in-sample OR would have passed 3 cells; the cross-fitting fix (review blocker, A1) prevented a false CONTINUE. Reading: the fourth instance of the same pattern (margins → per-site table; D1 → fixed rate; D2 → per-type plan): the value lies in detecting the event and in a pre-planned response, not in fine-grained online adaptation

Prior art (V96) and a correction to V94. P1's mechanism (incident detection, then a plan or mode switch for ramp metering) is prior art (Sheu & Chang 2007; Dabiri & Kulcsár 2014; Wu 2014; FHWA plans; Gao & Xu 2026 in SUMO). Viable only reframed as "How much incident information does ramp metering need?", with strong always-on baselines and sensitivity rows. P2's statistics are known (Cameron et al. 2016; van Hasselt 2010; Smith & Winkler 2006); it becomes a methods section of P1 with bracketing. Correction to V94: ORX is a double estimator and biased low, so per-incident headroom over the per-type plan lies between ~0–1 % and 5–40 % and was not shown to reach 10 %; the STOP stands under the rule as registered. Summary: docs/research/prior_art_P1_P2.md

V14110-21Gate outcome: work-zone plant plus a fixed actuator
full entry
Gate outcome: work-zone plant plus a fixed actuator (author choice on the V140 results; the V133 fallback). Plant WZ: 3 upstream lanes (entry 200 m, meter approach and storage 600 m to the signal, 200 m to the drop), a 3→2 zipper lane drop, a 2-lane work-zone bottleneck of 400 m, then 200 m to the exit; 23 m/s; same edge ids 1-5; meter across all 3 lanes. Incidents: lane closure = stopped blocker on lane 4_1 inside the 2-lane bottleneck (capacity really falls to one lane); slowdown = edge 4 at 5 m/s. Actuator fix (T0): a release-tracking signal. It counts vehicles crossing the stop line and keeps them on the commanded cumulative count: green ≥ 6 s, then amber 5 s and red ≥ 2 s once the count is ahead; green again once 3 vehicles (1 per lane) are owed; the owed count is capped; it rests in green at or above R_REST. Seeds: calibration on 7,430,010-019 (stage 1, same 54-configuration grid and selection rule); tool checks on 7,430,100-149 with the gate's check structure. Criteria unchanged, with one adaptation forced by the geometry: T1b's field QDF range [1,770, 2,330] applies per lane of the 2-lane bottleneck. Demand levels and constant-rate grids are scaled to the new capacity (q_near = calibration pre-queue flow, rounded to 50 veh/h; T1f grid 0.6-1.0 × QDF; T0 rates 0.4/0.6/0.8 × QDF). BN4-LC is closed for lane-closure incidents (V140)

WZ calibration stage 1: no configuration passes (540 runs, code ef56a96, seeds 7,430,010-019; the first launch failed at EXEC before any run because exFAT drops the exec bit; relaunched through bash, logged in RELAUNCH.json). The chain stopped before the tool checks, as the gate requires. Two causes. (1) Measurement: the code detects breakdown from min(edge-3, edge-4) loop speed, which deviates from the gate's "edge-4 loops" (this also applies to the BN4 stage-1 numbers in V139, now disclosed). On WZ the edge-3 loops sit 20 m before the drop, inside the 100-m zipper merging zone, so they flag "breakdown" when merging starts (about 3,300 veh/h) while the exit flow still rises to 4,200-4,560 veh/h: the Krauss rows show negative drops and are not interpretable. (2) Physics: IDM with the Flow parameters gives a per-lane QDF of about 1,160 veh/h, far below the field range. Summary: docs/research/results/p1c_wz_calibration_stage1.json. Decision on how to proceed is pending

V15210-21Where RL can still add value: synthesis v0
full entry
Where RL can still add value: synthesis v0 (author: "understand how the DRL/RL could still work and see what we can bring new"). Inputs: six full-text thesis reviews (docs/research/lit_reviews/, page-cited, key claims spot-checked) and a web sweep of about 45 papers. Result: docs/research/rl_value_synthesis_v0.md. Findings: no thesis or paper found calibrates or varies the capacity drop or beats a tuned feedback controller on mobility. On BN4 the best RL equals ALINEA at 40 % AVs, with lane changes off (Vinitsky et al. 2023, checked in the arXiv full text, lines 623 and 821). RL's documented value is adaptation and robustness, safety and responsiveness (I-24 MARVEL), CAV smoothing (non-RL controllers competitive) and repair of mis-tuned control. Candidate contributions: C1 operating map of headroom against capacity-drop size; C2 calibrated replication of the BN4/Flow RL results; C3 adaptation gain of a learned scheduler for tuned ALINEA under imperfect detection and day mix; C4-C7 riskier or outside the line. Claude's recommendation: C1 + C2 as paper_1 (methods / replication), C3 as paper 2 if C1 shows headroom. Novelty claims are "not found in this sweep", to be checked in WoS / Scopus. Pending author decision

V15410-28Grid flaw in T1f (V147) logged; H1 re-run drafted
full entry
Grid flaw in T1f (V147) logged; H1 re-run drafted (author: "yes, go ahead"). The T1f constant grid was 0.6-1.0 × QDF (1,150-1,950 veh/h, v5b/p1c/bn4_slow_test.py:44). It never entered the band between the discharge flow (1,954 veh/h, V147) and the pre-queue flow (2,106 veh/h, V139), the only band where a constant meter can gain. The best rate sat on the grid's top edge, with tuning delay still falling, and T1f had no edge rule. At demand 2,100 veh/h, a 1,950 veh/h meter builds about the same queue as the breakdown it should prevent. T1f could therefore not pass as designed, so the V147 KILL is not valid evidence until H1 runs. The V149 (feedback) KILL is not affected by this flaw: those meters could exceed 1,950 veh/h. Context: on the old plant with Flow IDM (drop 50-54 %, V139), the best tuned controller cut median delay by 21-43 % vs no control (P1b Table 2, difference of medians). Also corrected: the "11-22 %" cited in V149 is the type plan's gain over presence-only control (V113), not a gain over no control. Draft docs/research/protocols/p1c_h1_grid.md: grid up to 2,150 veh/h with an edge rule; tuning seeds 7,430,220-229, evaluation seeds 7,430,640-659; slowdown cell binding (T1f bar, rel ≥ 10 %), clean-day cell report-only. Pending author approval of the criteria and seeds, then a design review

V15510-28H1 design review: do not run H1 as drafted; V154 corrected; a T1d counter bug found
full entry
H1 design review: do not run H1 as drafted; V154 corrected; a T1d counter bug found (author: "Do the review"). Review docs/research/reviews/p1c_h1_design_review.md: four read-only lenses with an adversarial verifier each and a completeness critic, no simulations. 36 verified findings, all confirmed (1 blocker, 12 major), plus 6 unverified critic points. (1) Blocker M1: in the slowdown cell the incident is the binding bottleneck. Recomputed from the stored V147 runs, median exit during the incident: NC 1,173, c1950 1,164 veh/h. After it clears, the queue between the meter and edge 5 discharges at QDF for any constant rate at or above QDF (NC 1,957, c1950 1,961 veh/h). A rate in the band can act only between 300 s and the onset: median 72 s on the planned tuning seeds and 153 s on the evaluation seeds. NC broke down before the onset on 1 of 20 V147 seeds. The H1 slowdown verdict is therefore close to predetermined. (2) Corrections to V154: the grid was the approved V146 design, carried over from V141's WZ rescale, not a code bug. V139's BN4 grid had reached 2,000 veh/h. The V147 slowdown KILL for constant metering stands, on the measured 1,950 point plus the mechanism; V154's 'not valid evidence' is withdrawn. The band's upper bound on fresh seeds with the gate detector is about 2,064 veh/h, not 2,106 (V139 used the old detector), and the band is empty on 4 of 10 seeds. The BN4 plant failed T1a in V147 (60 % of seeds in range against 75 %), so 'realistic plant' in V149 and V154 is not established. (3) Bug after results (CLAUDE.md rule): the emergency-stop regex at v5b/p1c/episode.py:31 expects lane='...', but SUMO writes on lane '...'. It matched none of the about 21 million stored warning lines (verifier; one line rechecked by Claude). So the T1d 'forced stops' of V140 and V147 came from a counter that cannot count. Surviving evidence: the libsumo emergency_stops counter is 0 in all 175 V147 and 1,120 T1g runs (verifier's computation), but it is not verified to cover stops at a red meter. Fix and re-derivation pending. (4) Critic X1 (estimate, not verified): a fluid estimate puts the ceiling of any mainline meter, RL included, in this cell at about 6-10 %, at or below the 10 % bar. The options go to the author

V15810-29Vehicle-parameter randomization, step 1
full entry
Vehicle-parameter randomization, step 1 (author answers to the four V157 questions, side chat). (1) Sourced rows only. Into the plant now: the note's rows with status "sourced distribution" (docs/research/driver_params_hdv_cav_v0.md §4): HDV-car tau (UK close-following net-gap CDF [1], to be digitised; its mean is the calibration knob), HDV-car actionStepLength and sigma (per-vehicle Krauss fits, US arterial [50]; weak transfer to freeways), ACC tau 1.1 / 1.6 / 2.2 s at 50.4 / 18.5 / 31.1 % [18], CACC tau cars 0.6 / 0.7 / 0.9 / 1.1 s at 57 / 24 / 7 / 12 % [18] and trucks 0.6 / 0.9 / 1.2 / 1.5 / 1.8 s at 26.0 / 10.3 / 43.3 / 8.0 / 12.5 % [19], CACC latency and loss from the field percentiles [123][62] (emulated in the libsumo layer, since SUMO's CACC assumes ideal communication), and the detector-fault rates of §2.7 for the sensor model. Every other parameter keeps the V156 value or the SUMO 1.27.1 default. HDV model stays Krauss (implied: the sourced sigma and action-step rows are Krauss fits; not asked separately). (2) CAV classes: ACC, CACC and ALKS-like automated vehicles. The automated class has rule rows only (R157 [22]), so it is an explicit exception to (1). (3) ACC gains: the original controller gains (string-unstable at short gaps, as in field data [15][59][60]), not SUMO's damped defaults; exact 1.27.1 attribute names and values to be confirmed in the SUMO source before use. (4) Seeds ("OK, use the seeds"; read as no new range): every per-vehicle draw comes from the episode seed of the approved v5.B block, on its own RNG stream, so all arms see the same vehicles (CRN) and each seed keeps its role (calibration, tuning, validation, test). Constraint from the note: tau ≥ actionStepLength per vehicle (resample the pair, report the rejection share); an action step above the 0.1 s step switches SUMO to ballistic update. Open: O1 desired speeds: V156 (author assumption) stays unless the author swaps it for the sourced UK speedFactor (cars normc(0.98, 0.12); trucks mean 87.8 km/h, SD 5.5 [90]); O2 CAV penetration and class shares (needed before calibration); O3 automated-vehicle time gap above 60 km/h: R157 para. 5.2.3.3 defers to the national rules of the country of operation (checked in the 01 series text), and the country is not chosen; O4 the [1] Fig. 5 CDF must be digitised or recomputed. Consequence: with V156, one recalibration (V139, T1a/T1b) before any controller test

The collided vehicles will not be teleported and stay there for 30 to 60 minutes like in reality. This will disrupt the traffic, and this will help us"). V16610-29Crash-model evidence v0
full entry
Crash-model evidence v0 (V165 (1); one research agent, ultracode off). Note docs/research/crash_model_evidence_v0.md: 107 claims, 52 sources, access tags FT / ABS / DATA / DERIVED; many freeway papers read as abstracts only. Claude re-checked the key source: Orsini et al. 2020 (IET ITS 14(9)), radar TTC at 19 cross-sections of two motorways in north-eastern Italy, observed rear-end crashes inside the 95 % CI at about 90 % of sections. Readings: (a) compute same-lane rear-end TTC ourselves every second from getLeader; SUMO's SSM runtime value device.ssm.minTTC is the minimum since the encounter began and also covers other-lane foes (libsumo 1.27.1 test: 19 times more seconds below 3 s); (b) TTC < 1.5 s is the most used threshold (SSAM default) but no freeway crash-validated threshold exists; 1.0 s and 3.0 s as sensitivity arms; (c) published crash-to-conflict ratios span 1:1,000 to 1:100,000 (mostly Swedish urban intersections), so a severity-weighted p (shape from an EVT tail fitted to no-control runs, one scale tuned to the target) is recommended, constant p as a sensitivity arm; (d) the V165 target (P(≥1 crash/day) = 25 %, λ 0.288/day) on about 1 km is 8-14 crashes per million veh-km against about 0.6 on US urban freeways (all reported crashes, Caltrans) and 0.028 injury crashes on GB motorways: a stress regime, to be labelled so; (e) 30-60 min blockage fits HCM incident defaults (means 35-68 min, US); 57 % of GB motorway injury collisions involve two vehicles; (f) UK motorway weekday profile (WebTRIS, 10 sites): peak hour 7.75 % of daily traffic, so about 18,000 veh/day puts the peak at 1,400 veh/h; (g) no study validates SUMO conflicts against freeway crashes

No-control reference days, first pass: Layer A not clean (V167; seeds 7,430,040-049, 10 days of 20,000 vehicles each, about 17 min per day; summary docs/research/results/fleet_day_cal_v0.json). First run (code 6448b0d) had a breakdown-detector bug: an empty lane counted as speed 0, so night hours looked like jams; fixed (vehicle-weighted speed, empty intervals count as free) and re-measured on the same seeds (code 1310ae3, identical simulation). Baseline: 0 teleports, all drained, no SUMO errors, but 3 SUMO collision events in 10 days (counter shows 6: both vehicles), all a human car rear-ending an ACC or ALKS car at 7-13 m/s in queues; emergency braking at 9 m/s² about 900 per day, per 1,000 vehicles: HDV car 2.0, truck 1.1, ACC 85, CACC 72, ALKS 91; 28-40 % of the CAV events within 5 s of insertion, the rest at the queue tail on edges 1-2. Capacity: 2-3 breakdowns per day (AM about 07:15, PM about 15:30), each about 4 h; pre-queue flow median 1,548 veh/h, QDF 1,208, drop median 22 % (12-30 %), above the 3-20 % T1a band; queues spill back to the network entrance. Conflicts: 226 rear-end encounters per day with TTC < 1.5 s, 2.2 per day below 1.0 s, lowest TTC 0.21 s; a GPD fit at 1.5 s (shape 0.045, KS p 0.03) implies about 0.003 crashes per day, about 85 times below the 0.288 target. Variant CAV apparentDecel 9 m/s² (code ac36996): 1 collision event, more emergency braking (CAV 103-148 per 1,000), lower capacity (pre-queue 1,488, QDF 1,198); not adopted. Reading: the residual collisions follow CAV hard braking, caused by insertion behind a spilled-back queue and by SUMO's ACC approaching standing queues late. Options go to the author

V17010-29Second p1c measurement bug: an empty lane counts as speed 0
full entry
Second p1c measurement bug: an empty lane counts as speed 0 (reported by the side chat, confirmed by Claude from the code; impact not yet measured). v5b/p1c/episode.py:76-77 _mean maps getLastIntervalMeanSpeed = −1 (no vehicle in the interval) to 0 and averages over lanes. On a 2-lane loop pair, one empty lane halves the mean: at 23 m/s it gives 11.5 m/s, which is the breakdown threshold (calibrate.py:110, 0.5 × FREE). So the 'up' / e3 / e4 speed series can show spurious slow intervals at low or uneven lane flow. Exposure: breakdown time, pre-queue flow, QDF and drop wherever they come from these series (V139, V140, V142-V145, V147 T1a/T1b) and the recovery counts in V155 M1. Not affected: the meter's occupancy input (an empty lane gives occupancy 0, which is correct); exit counts; delays; V155 M1's exit-flow figures. Stored series keep only the lane means, so the size of the effect needs re-runs. Together with the T1d regex bug (V155): one bug-fix batch (fix both, add unit tests, re-run the affected checks once and log both outcomes), pending author approval. Seeds: 7,430,040-049 now belong to the side chat (V165, V167); the V153 plan's use of them for a G2 gap fill is void

(1) bn4x, ALKS on SUMO ACC: 4 SUMO collision events (counter 8), all a human car or truck rear-ending a CAV; emergency braking per 1,000 vehicles: ACC 252, CACC 129, ALKS 258, HDV car 2.0; pre-queue 1,488 veh/h, QDF 1,209, drop 18 % (10-26 %). V17310-29Plant and crash-rule choices
full entry
Plant and crash-rule choices (author, on V172). (1) Variant B: bn4x (3 km longer entry), every CAV class on IDM with its sourced time gaps (ACC 1.1 / 1.6 / 2.2 s, CACC 0.6-1.1 s, ALKS 1.6 s); replaces SUMO's ACC and CACC models from V158 and makes the V164 ACC-gain choice moot. Limitation to state: CACC is IDM with short gaps, without car-to-car cooperation. (2) Crash rule: only encounters with a human follower (HDV car or truck) can become crashes; all followers as a sensitivity arm. Claude's proposal kept: chance per encounter (TTC < 1.5 s) rising linearly as its lowest TTC falls, one scale set so that P(≥ 1 crash per no-control reference day) = 25 %; constant chance and the 1.0 / 3.0 s thresholds as sensitivity arms
Authorauthor, on V172V174 Layer B crash process built and validated
V17410-29Layer B crash process built and validated
full entry
Layer B crash process built and validated (V173 rule; code 475edcc; v5b/fleet/crash.py, tests/test_fleet_crash.py; summary docs/research/results/fleet_crash_validation_v0.json). Calibration on the 10 crash-free days of V172 (B): human followers, TTC < 1.5 s, linear, k = 0.00382; 1,262 encounters per day; largest chance per encounter 0.34 %; P(≥ 1 crash) 21-30 % per day, mean 25 %, expected 0.29 crashes per day. Sensitivity arms (same days): constant k 0.000229; u 3.0 s linear 6.5e-5; u 1.0 s linear 0.259 with only 3 encounters per day (thin arm); all followers at 1.5 s linear 0.0017. A crash: both vehicles brake at their emergency deceleration to a stop, no lane changes, U(30, 60) min, then removed; teleporting off (--time-to-teleport -1). CRN: one uniform per encounter from (seed, follower, leader, start second). Live check on the same 10 seeds: the first crash matched the offline replay of the crash-free records to the second and vehicle on all 3 crash days (…046 12:54, …048 08:08, …049 08:36), and the 7 crash-free days reproduced their crash-free hash. Secondary crashes behind the first on 2 days (23-26 min later). 0 SUMO collisions, 0 teleports, all drained, arrived + removed = generated; the runner's health codes H-E2 / H-R1 / H-R5 on crash days are the expected effect of removals and blocked vehicles. Finding: crashes happen at queue tails on the 4-lane entry, upstream of the 1-lane bottleneck, so their effect on delay is small when the bottleneck already limits flow (mean HDV-car delay +8 % on …046, about 0 % on …048 and …049). Crash lane and position are recorded from now on. Also seen: on …048 the AM and PM jams merge into one 13.4 h breakdown

Nonlinear mechanisms of real freeways: evidence v0 (V175; two research agents, ultracode off). Notes docs/research/nonlinear_flow_mechanisms_v0.md (about 107 claims) and docs/research/nonlinear_driver_exogenous_mechanisms_v0.md (106 claims, 35 sources); tags FT / ABS / DERIVED, unopened leads marked [VERIFY]. Claude re-checked two key sources: Zhang & Levinson 2004 (TRR 1883), 27 Twin Cities bottlenecks, flow drop 2-11 %, long-run mean QDF 2,016 and pre-queue flow 2,124 pcu/h/lane; Knoop, Hoogendoorn & Adams 2009 (EJTIR 9(4)) Table 5, 90 Dutch incidents, remaining capacity factor 0.36 (SD 0.14) with 1 of 3 lanes blocked, 0.18 with 2 of 3, rubbernecking 0.69, remaining-lane efficiency 0.54. Readings for the fleet plant (bn4x, V172 B): (a) its drop (18 %, 8-26 %) is above the field cluster (2-11 %, mean about 5 %) and its 1-lane pre-queue flow (about 1,450-1,550 veh/h) is about 30 % below field per-lane values, so it needs recalibration before any controller test (planned in V157: calibrate the means, keep the sourced shapes); (b) in SUMO the open lanes beside a crash run at full efficiency, against 0.54 in the field, so crashes are too mild; (c) missing mechanisms with field support: stochastic breakdown (Weibull capacity, shape 10-20; to be measured, not added), on-ramp merges with bounded meters (storage, maximum wait, 240-900 veh/h), off-ramp spillback and interacting bottlenecks, level-dependent VSL compliance (an enforced 40 km/h limit still carried 1,942 veh/h/lane for 17 min, Soriguera 2017), weather and darkness (rain about −10 % capacity, darkness −3 to −9 %), grades and sags, detector faults (35-40 % of California loops failed on a typical day); (d) stop-and-go wave speed and period of the plant are unmeasured (field −16 to −20 km/h, about 10 min); (e) our IDM CAVs are probably more string-stable than production ACC. Order of work goes to the author

V17710-29Fleet plant recalibration: protocol, fixed before any run
full entry
Fleet plant recalibration: protocol, fixed before any run (author: "yes, start it", on V176 (a)). Field capacities are measured on human traffic, so the calibration uses a human-only fleet (HDV cars 92.5 %, trucks 7.5 %, V156-V159 attributes); the 50 % CAV mix (V160-V161, V173) is then re-run with the chosen human parameters and its capacity and drop are predictions, reported, not tuned. Plant bn4x, step 0.1 s, all green, no crashes. Demand: the V139 ramp (300 s at 1,200 veh/h, ramp to 2,400 over 1,200 s, hold 1,200 s), measured with the V139 rule (calibrate.measure) at free speed 100 km/h and a vehicle-weighted loop speed. Knobs (V157: shapes stay sourced, only means move): HDV-car tau scale c ∈ {0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 1.0} (multiplies every drawn tau, so mean 0.69-1.15 s; tau ≥ action step kept), merge ∈ {zip20, zip100}, HDV-car accel ∈ {2.6 (SUMO default), 2.0 (middle of the sourced 1.8-2.2 m/s² range)}; 20 configurations × seeds 7,430,040-049 = 200 runs. Pass: median drop in [2 %, 11 %] (Zhang & Levinson 2004, 27 bottlenecks) with ≥ 75 % of seeds in that range; median QDF in the T1b band [1,770, 2,330] veh/h; 0 SUMO collisions and 0 teleports in every run. Selection: fewest non-default knobs (defaults c = 1.0, zip100, accel 2.6), then median drop closest to 5 % (the Twin Cities mean), then higher median QDF. If nothing passes, report and stop for the author

Cause found: SUMO's zipper merge caps throughput at fine steps; stage-2 protocol (V179). Step check on the V139-like human plant (code 5cf9aeb, seeds 7,430,040-049): QDF 1,954 (0.5 s Euler), 1,817 (0.5 s ballistic), 1,345 (0.25 s), 1,364 (0.2 s), 1,373 / 1,345 (0.1 s Euler / ballistic). By the V179 rule the Euler hypothesis is rejected (0.5 s ballistic stays high). Isolation test (scratch, not calibration seeds; summary added to docs/research/results/fleet_calib_human_v0.json): a 1-lane queue released by a signal discharges 2,520 veh/h at 0.1 s and 2,364 at 0.5 s, so Krauss itself is fine; a 2 → 1 zipper merge gives 1,344 at 0.1 s and 1,932 at 0.5 s, unchanged by visibility (20-300 m) or jmTimegapMinor (0-0.5 s); a lane-end merge (the dropped lane has no connection, so drivers must change lanes) gives 2,520 at 0.1 s and 2,124 at 0.5 s. Reading: the zipper junction model limits merge throughput to about 1,350 veh/h at steps ≤ 0.25 s; whether this is a SUMO bug is unverified. Stage-2 protocol, fixed before it runs: as V177 (human-only, bn4x, step 0.1 s, V139 ramp, seeds 7,430,040-049, same pass rule and selection) but merge = laneend at both drops; knobs tau scale c ∈ {0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 1.0} × accel ∈ {2.6, 2.0} = 10 configurations, 100 runs; defaults for selection c = 1.0, accel 2.6

Squeeze-in rule at the merge: test fixed before it runs (author "ok" to Claude's plan: test the squeeze-in rule, fall back to teleporting off if it causes collisions). Rule (v5b/fleet/merge.py RampMerge, all values assumptions): each whole second, a ramp vehicle that has stood (speed < 2 m/s) in the last 60 m of the acceleration lane for ≥ 10 s changes to the lane on its left with SUMO's safe-gap check skipped (TraCI lane-change mode bits 8-9 = 1, so only overlaps are avoided), when the left follower crawls (< 3 m/s) and the vehicle fits where it stands: its own minGap clear ahead, and behind it the follower's minGap plus the follower's stopping distance at its normal deceleration (so a space of at least car length + 2 × 2.5 m). Adopt the squeeze if, with it, all 10 seeds drain with 0 SUMO collisions and the median number of ramp vehicles waiting > 60 s is below the median without it. Otherwise option 2 (no squeeze, teleporting off), if the off arm drains with 0 collisions on all 10 seeds; if neither, stop for the author. Either way the plant then runs with teleporting off, and Layer A's 0-teleport check becomes: drained, 0 SUMO collisions, merge waits reported. Claude, result or own callSee entryV199 Incident passing zone: design and calibration fixed before building
V19910-30Incident passing zone: design and calibration fixed before building
full entry
Incident passing zone: design and calibration fixed before building (author "Go" to the V198 next step). Target (Knoop, Hoogendoorn & Adams 2009, EJTIR 9(4), Table 5, read in full in V176): queue discharge at the incident site over the normal queue discharge F = 0.36 (SD 0.14) with 1 of 3 lanes blocked; efficiency of the remaining lanes η = F / (open lanes / lanes) = 0.54 with 1 or 2 of 3 blocked. Mechanism (v5b/fleet/incident.py; values are assumptions unless sourced): while a crash blocks a lane, human drivers (HDV cars and trucks; CAVs keep their gaps) within 100 m upstream (along the road, across edges) and 100 m downstream of the front crashed vehicle, on any lane, drive with their tau multiplied by f; set at whole seconds, restored when they leave the zone or the crash is removed; f = 1 is a no-op. One knob: speeds fall by themselves, a simplification of "longer headway and lower speed". Calibration: a straight 3-lane road (100 km/h, 5 km), the V187 human fleet with plant v188 driver knobs, constant demand 5,000 veh/h (above the 3,588 veh/h two lanes would discharge at full efficiency, below 3 × the V187 pre-queue flow 1,938); after 600 s the first human vehicle on the right lane to reach 3,000 m crashes alone (V163 braking and lane-change rule), blocked for 1,800 s. Discharge = vehicles over a loop 300 m downstream (all lanes) from 300 s after the crash to its removal; valid if the 60-s speed at a loop 500 m upstream is below 70 km/h (Knoop's congestion threshold; no vehicles counts as congested) in ≥ 90 % of the window. η = discharge / (2 × 1,794), with 1,794 veh/h the plant's per-lane queue discharge (V187). Grid f ∈ {1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 4.0} × seeds 7,430,040-049 (60 runs). Choice: the f whose median η over valid seeds is closest to 0.54; it passes if that median is within 0.54 ± 0.05 with ≥ 8 valid seeds; if none passes but two values bracket 0.54, one refinement grid of three values between them; otherwise stop for the author. Report-only rows at the chosen f (10 seeds each): zone ± 300 m; crash in the left lane; a 2-lane road with 1 lane blocked (demand 3,300 veh/h; F about 0.27 from η, HCM 2010 0.35) at the chosen f and at 1.0. Adoption: plant v199 = v190 + the zone. Crash-free days are unchanged by construction; the 10 V198 crash-live days are re-run (9 hashes must match, the …041 first crash must match) and the crash day's delay effect is reported

V20910-31The dry-day collision of the V207 batch is a SUMO lane-change artefact
full entry
The dry-day collision of the V207 batch is a SUMO lane-change artefact (stop rule of V207: 1 SUMO collision in the first 63 finished days, dry seed 7,431,093; author "yes" to a diagnostic replay). The replay with the frozen code 8d74cf5 reproduced it to the step and vehicle (t = 29,619.4-29,619.5 s, lane 3_1 at 797 m, about 400 m before the 3 → 2 lane drop). Sequence: an ALKS vehicle (IDM, tau 1.6 s) stopped at the end of the queue on lane 3_2, which ends at the lane drop, changed to 3_1 at 0.07 m/s (strategic, urgent) at t = 29,619.1, leaving about 0.15 m (beyond minGap) to the HDV car behind it; that car (Krauss, tau 0.549 s, actionStepLength 0.5 s, the V187 calibrated action step) had stood still with its leader 7.4 m ahead and at its action point t = 29,619.0 chose +2.56 m/s²; it could not react before its next action point and reached 1.28 m/s before braking. No physical contact (corrected the same day from "struck … overlap 0.07 m"): the closest bumper-to-bumper distance was 2.36 m (t = 29,619.7 s), i.e. the car entered the 2.5 m minGap by up to 0.15 m. SUMO 1.27.1 flags that as a collision here because --collision.mingap-factor is left at its default (the car-following model's collisionMinGapFactor), so every earlier "0 collisions" check also counted minGap intrusions. LC2013 judged the gap safe from the follower's current speed, not from its planned acceleration. Neither the passing zone, the weather code nor the ramp merge acts there. The batch keeps running; the acceptance rule (strategy row A, docs/research/weather_plant_strategy_v0.md) goes to the author

V21110-31Collision rule: physical contacts and minGap intrusions counted apart
full entry
Collision rule: physical contacts and minGap intrusions counted apart (author "A OK" to Claude's recommendation after V209). A SUMO collision event is a physical contact unless its bumper-to-bumper distance stayed above 0 over all its steps; an event without a distance counts as contact. Any contact keeps the V207 stop rule (stop for the author). minGap intrusions are counted, reported per weather state and per controller arm, and disclosed; an arm whose intrusion rate is above no control's (paired CI excluding 0) gets a safety flag and its cells are not claimed without the author. SUMO options are unchanged (--collision.mingap-factor default), so dynamics and hashes are unchanged. Code: day._bumper (collider front to victim back = getLeader distance + collider minGap, the formula checked on the V209 trace) per collision step, _first_steps keeps the event's smallest distance, contact_counts adds contacts and mingap_intrusions to every day result; tests/test_fleet_collisions.py. Runs from frozen code before this commit (the V207 batch) record speeds only; their events are settled by replay (V209: the one dry event is an intrusion, 2.36 m). Rejected: counting only contacts in SUMO (--collision.mingap-factor 0; loses the near-miss record), counting every SUMO event as a collision (treats a 2.4 m near-miss as a crash), new lane-change parameters or a shorter human action step (re-runs V187-V207 and breaks the only passing V187 configuration), a CAV lane-end gap rule (unsourced, re-runs every mixed-fleet result), dropping the day (seed cherry-picking). V207 phase 2 stop-rule fields: 90/90 days drained, 0 teleports, 0 SUMO errors, 1 event (the V209 intrusion)

Q2: 3 ALINEA points at alinea_3 and 3 PI-ALINEA points at the drop loop; red rest while metering, one green per waiting vehicle, 5-s amber at metering onset, queue law at 150 s inside the 210-s backstop. Q3: the I cell uses a stalled human vehicle at 650 m on lane 3_1 at 16:00 (normal braking, 45 min, f = 3) instead of the V202 crash, if it passes the V199 η check (0.54 ± 0.05); else the V202 crash. Q4: main seeds from 7,430,230 (n = 10, 15 or 20 by the power rule), C1 on the next 10, twin SUMO seeds at demand seed + 5,000 (7,435,000-7,435,999 SUMO-seed-only, never demand seeds), stage 0 on 7,430,040-049 and 7,435,040-049, E2 tuning on the E1 main seeds, E2 evaluation reserved at 7,430,660-689. Q5: one per-day decision oracle that may choose no control, counted only after a replicate on twin SUMO seeds; tuned passes replicate only if their noise floor ≥ 5 %. Q6: MC* always (a cascade when both laws use the drop loop), the edge rule, the C1 extension with fresh-only rel ≥ 0.05. Q7: a KILL means no gain ≥ 15 % with probability ≥ 0.80 (n set by the measured noise, upper 80 % bound); the 10 % bar is unchanged. Q8: V211 flag by an exact one-sided binomial test of pooled intrusion counts against no control (α = 0.05); contacts still stop the work. Compute: about 34-38 h expected at n = 10, about 69 h at n = 20

V23411-01Re-review of the fix diff and its fixes
full entry
Re-review of the fix diff and its fixes (author: "High, ultracode on"; workflow over 579e278..HEAD: 4 area reviewers, one refuting skeptic per area, a completeness critic; 11 findings survived, 0 in the actuators). Fixed, each with a test that fails on the old code: (1) the R/I prefix check compared per-cell MC* controllers and would block the verdict whenever the cells tune differently; it now skips keys whose ctrl differs. (2) Idle replacement took the lowest idle setpoint first, which could remove p0.95 and silence the §8 edge rule; the highest goes first now, and the edge rule falls back to the grid's middle setpoint. (3) §10.6 stop rules were never applied to C1 and C2 runs; final_verdict now refuses on them, and a batch refuses to start while STOP.txt exists. (4) The smoke check and every resume reused runs from other code; each day file now carries code (a hash of the simulation sources), matches() compares it, and smoke runs go to a folder per code. (5) O_off could count after a flagged tuned pass under Rule 2; it now needs no tuned pass at all (§9.5). (6) Post-hoc power used the 10-pair s_U at n = 20; now n pairs. (7) Gain-check RMS paired each active minute with the occupancy one minute early; corrected; choices unchanged (ALINEA K_R 70: RMS 10.20 vs 10.84 and 11.73; MTFC K_I 0.02). (8) A failed attempt cut short by a stop is now kept (ATTEMPT1_FAILED.txt; one attempt on resume). (9) day batch --forced works again. (10) Noise floors and the global null took 12 points and 6 per family; e1 report --wave floors recomputes them at the frozen grid. (11) Disclosure: the T0 rate check pools 5 clean minutes, not necessarily adjacent (the code's reading of '5-min interval' since V220); the clock-interval values are now reported too (ratio_clock). Stage-0 runs lack code, so a resume would refuse them (archive first); their reports are unaffected

V23911-01E1-lite L1 verification
full entry
E1-lite L1 verification (author "Extra High, ultracode on"; workflow with 4 checkers, one refuting skeptic each and a completeness critic; read-only, no simulation; scripts in the session scratchpad verify_l1/). (1) An independent script reproduces L1_report.json exactly (rel; the CIs with the §7.1 bootstrap seed; oracle 0.186; best ma/p0.85; UNCLEAR). The rule code matches e1_lite.md, and L2 pools 7,430,230-249 with no path collision. (2) Metric: per seed, every arm serves the same vehicles (same route file, all arrive, none removed, no teleports), so d_all changes are real time changes. TTT = N·D + a constant here, so TTT does not corroborate D independently. Served PM throughput is nearly degenerate on drained slices and can carry the wrong sign. (3) MTFC: no implementation artefact found. The drop loop stays at about twice the setpoint, b sits at b_min for 55-59 % of the slice, and the bottleneck discharges 1.9-3.0 % less in 16-19 h. The harm is saturation without authority on this plant; the micro-mechanism is a hypothesis. (4) ALINEA: the braking counts are reproduced (31/34/34, all on r_0). The stored outputs cannot attribute them to the V232 creep: 11 distinct events are CAV approaches at short queues, and 3 vehicles were measured at 7.3-13.6 m/s 1 s before braking. The gains are not driven by one seed (leave-one-out 0.081-0.093 for p0.85) and do not track braking. The ma/p0.85 mean-version rel is -0.011 (two seeds with large ramp and mainline losses). Meter waits over 240 s: 414-834 per run (V190 4-min limit). (5) Disclosure corrections: the best-of-9 noise floor under the global null is about +6.7 to +9.9 % at n = 10 and +5.0 to +7.3 % at n = 20 (the protocol said about +4 %). The observed L1 CI half-widths are 0.12-0.22 (the protocol said ±12 %). A slice rel of 0.10 ≈ a full-day rel of 0.086. (6) Code gaps, no effect on L1: stop_reasons omits ALKS allowed_mismatch (V226 rule; 0 in L1); lite_report has no code-id check; a STOP does not block the report; the reports run from the live repo (identical to 8eb212c until L2_report.json exists). (7) The §8 edge rule fires for ALINEA (0.75) and MTFC long. (8) The §10.3 loop tests on the L1 NC slices pass on 4/10 days (drop), 3/10 (dropend) and 4/10 (alinea spillback); calibration was validated on full days only.

full entry
E1-lite: four rules fixed before L2 is read (author, all four recommended options; L2 running, L2_report.json unread). (1) An ALINEA GO is a conditional GO: no confirmation and no build on it until the meter passes T0 and the V190 4-min wait question is settled. (2) An n = 20 UNCLEAR means no GO: the best arm's estimate is reported with its upper CI as the largest effect not excluded, E1 builds nothing on this plant, and the next step is chosen then. Approximate operating characteristics of the n = 20 rule (parametric MC, s 0.219): P(UNCLEAR) 0.72 with no effect, 0.76 at +5 %, 0.48 at +10 %; P(KILL \| no effect) about 0.24. (3) If the n = 20 best ALINEA point is 0.85 (the grid edge), ma/p0.75 runs on the same 20 seeds as a report-only map extension (best-of-10, disclosed). (4) A GO is confirmed on 7,430,260-279 (E1 reserve, n = 20, seed check before use), on the n = 20 best arm only; pass = rel ≥ 0.10 and lower CI > 0 on those seeds alone. The R outcomes on 7,430,230-249 have now been read, so a resumed E1 stage A on R cannot use them as unread main seeds. The n = 20 report gets report-only additions from separate code (the rule code stays frozen): per-block L1/L2 rel; diff, sign, mean version and harm label; the §7.2-7.5 flags including braking; all-lane and :m_0_0 braking; served throughput with its caveat; the slice loop tests; the corrected noise floor; the full-day conversion.

V24211-01E1-lite R: verified interpretation, inconclusive
full entry
E1-lite R: verified interpretation, inconclusive (author "Switched", Extra High with ultracode; workflow with 3 analysts (statistics, mechanism, strategy), one refuting skeptic each and a synthesis; no simulation; scripts in the session scratchpad interp_n20/). The n = 20 R result is inconclusive: neither a null nor a 5-8 % effect. (1) ALINEA 1.05 is +8.3 % [-0.5, +15.1] on the slice (mean version +5.2 %, 14/20 seeds; sign test p 0.058 one-sided, unadjusted). If ALINEA had no effect (MTFC as observed), the best arm reaches ≥ +8.3 % with P 0.21-0.23, so the data fit 'no effect' and '+8-10 %' about equally well. A true +10 % is not excluded for any ALINEA point. Distribution-free upper bounds reach about +18 % per arm and about +22 % for the family. Full day is about +7 % (upper about +13 %, × 0.858, approximate). The 0.85 L1 → L2 reversal is ordinary n = 10 noise (exact split test P 0.62); 10-seed tuning is optimistic by about +0.06 (cross-fit +0.024). (2) ALINEA 1.05's gain is a net mainline gain (+2,310 veh·h) partly paid for by ramp drivers (-575 veh·h). The breakdown does not shift (median t_b +7 min [-58.5, +38.5]). In 16-19 h the ALINEA law sets the rate in only 0.6-2.8 % of minutes; queue override or backstop sets it in 72.5-78.9 % (inference: the meter has little feedback authority in the jam). (3) Plant (inference): the PM queue is demand-driven (16-17 h demand 3,508 veh/h against a queue discharge of 3,141, +11.7 %). On these slices the protocol's capacity-drop statistic (9.0-9.6 %) sits at the level of in-queue noise (13.8 %; null simulation about 15 %). A perfectly timed meter limited to 4-min waits could recover only about 1-5 % by postponing the breakdown; that bound covers that channel only. (4) MTFC is robustly worse for this configuration (Bonferroni × 9 upper bounds -0.079 to -0.172): b sits at b_min in 56-61 % of the slice, it restricts flow before the breakdown, the breakdown starts 10-45 min earlier and lasts 47-69 min longer, and discharge is 1.8-2.7 % lower. b is clamped, so there is no windup. (5) Not shown: no-effect, a ceiling, anything about the I cell, other demand, rain, MC*, or CAV control in general. Untested: the upper grid edges (ALINEA 1.15 and MTFC long 1.15) and MC*. The 4-min wait breaches come mostly from the plant (39.8 % of NC ramp trips already exceed 240 s of delay).

Authorauthor, all four recommended options after V242V244 v199 capacity drop: not distinguishable from noise; T1 could not fail
V24411-01v199 capacity drop: not distinguishable from noise; T1 could not fail
full entry
v199 capacity drop: not distinguishable from noise; T1 could not fail (V243(4); workflow with 2 independent methods, one refuting skeptic each and a judge; analysis only, 20 full-day NC R days on 7,430,040-049 and their twins 7,435,040-049, plus 30 dry weather-plant NC days 7,431,080-109 as a variant check; scripts in the session scratchpad drop_check/). (1) The V220 T1 drop reproduces exactly (9.35 % on the base days; 10.2 % [8.5, 12.4] on all 20 days). (2) The same max-5 statistic gives a similar or larger value inside the queue: 13.0-14.2 % on a random in-queue window, and P - reference = -0.75 pp [-2.0, +1.0] against a count-corrected slow-only reference. With no drop at all, its null median is 10.8-12.65 % (p95 15-18 %), against the 2 % stop line, so T1 could not fail on this plant. (3) The protocol's 'pre' hour overlaps an earlier drop-loop episode on 20/20 days. With clean free-flow windows, the max-based versions are +0.6 to +3.3 % (biased upward by the max) and the sustained 10-15 min means are -2.5 to -6.4 % (at or below QDF). No capacity drop is shown; an upper bound of about 3 % at 5-min resolution cannot be excluded. (4) The lane drop is the active bottleneck on 20/20 days. Breakdowns start stochastically at 0.9-1.0 × QDF (hazard per 15 min 0.26-0.31 there, 0.02-0.05 below 0.9 × QDF), and 39-40 of 42 clean onsets start below QDF. (5) Consequences (inference): V220's T1 pass carries no evidence of a drop. On v199, holding the free state means metering below QDF, so control can only move where the queue sits and how delay is spread, not recover a drop; this fits V242. 9.4 % (and the v190 figure of about 11 %) must not be quoted as a capacity drop; if it is quoted at all, it is 'the protocol's max-5 statistic, about 11-13 % under a no-drop null'. Any future T1 needs a like-for-like statistic, with its threshold set against a no-drop null before data (author decision when a plant study is next planned). Open hypothesis: SUMO lane-end merging sets the breakdown at 0.9-1.0 × QDF (no per-lane data to test it).

Prior art A: the drop axis itself is covered in part (Ke et al. 2021, DRL VSL at 5/8.4/15 % drop in a CTM, against no control only; Jin & Jin 2015, feedback VSL across the drop size, no gain at a drop of 0). The Vinitsky et al. 2023 checkpoints need Python 3.7, TF 1.15, ray 0.7.4 and SUMO 1.1.0, and each stored training run took 47-95 h. Prior art B: SUMO RL merging studies exist (e.g. Yan et al. 2024, Z-Merge 2025, Trust-MARL 2025), all against no control, SUMO defaults, untuned rules or other RL. Not found: a tuned non-learning cooperative-merge opponent against RL with paired statistics and safety as the primary outcome. Expected mobility effects are small; reported benefits come below breakdown and mostly at high CAV shares; gap protection is needed. Red flag (from stored runs, as read by the A reviewer; not re-checked by Claude): BN4 at IDM a = 1.0 discharges exactly 900 veh/h on every seed (7-8 vehicles per 30 s, no seed-to-seed variance), so the V139 50-54 % drop may be a zipper-junction timing artefact at the 0.5-s step; this bears on the BN4 DRL PASS (day-pattern D5.10) and on the P1/P1b gains. Drafts: A 17 and B 18 author decisions; the critic's 7 high-impact cross-track issues are open (Vinitsky-first order, two CAV definitions, invalid/teleport rules, the V211 contact classifier for lateral events, B's demand ladder built on human-only capacity, B's 25 % share where prior art predicts a null, the seed ledger).

V25511-02Stage-0 audit and archive re-read (verified)
full entry
Stage-0 audit and archive re-read (verified) (author "Extra High, ultracode on"; workflow: 3 checks, each with a refuting skeptic, then a strategist and a critic; read-only, no simulation; scripts in the session scratchpad interp_s0/). (1) Stage 0 stands: an independent recompute reproduces stage0_report.json exactly, and A-UNTESTABLE(BN4) holds under 12-13 estimator variants and a speed-based onset. Corrections to V249/V254: the zipper + Flow-IDM discharge is near-deterministic (about 900 veh/h, a 4-s headway, 912 at 0.25 s), so 'step-locked' names the wrong cause; it is step-stable, passes criteria 2-4 and fails only criterion 1 (no seed spread); 0/20 of its runs drained. Only zipper + Krauss is step-dependent (1,956 vs 1,344 veh/h). τ_null(10) is -0.3 / 2.2 / 6.3 %. Lane-end IDM a = 2.6 was never loaded past its discharge (peak demand 1,884 / 1,642 against about 2,120-2,200 veh/h), so its drop is untested. The -3.6 to -7.7 % drops come from transient first activations on the demand ramp. 'No real drop' is supported only for lane-end Krauss. Lane-end IDM a = 1.0 deadlocked on 4/10 seeds at 0.5 s and on none at 0.25 s. null_base used an undisclosed all-rows fallback, and the e4 loops overcount by 2-88. (2) D5.10 (BN4 DRL pass) and R6 ran on that zipper + Flow-IDM plant (archive vsl_lab bn4, unchanged since 920ff71; lane changes off; 0.5 s; teleport 300). D5.10's gain over no control (-49.3 %) rests on avoiding the 900 veh/h standing state: a constant 1,800 veh/h meter ties the DRL in the unperturbed regime (-0.79 s [-3.19, 2.86]), and all three R6+ learners have converged_c1 = false. Whether its regime wins over the tuned meters rest on the same state cannot be told, because the raw runs are deleted. The block start depends on the controller (a validity threat). (3) P1/P1b and C1 ran on the same plant (identical net and plant code at 85f7d34, 93ba655 and e7dd561). A fit to the no-control drains gives a 4.0-4.3 s headway in all 15 cells, and the drain holds 0.55-1.1 of the TTS gaps. C1 (V116): about half of the IP - PI gap is drain at 900 veh/h; in the window, IP vs PI is 11.7 % [6.5, 14.4], but PI is worse than no control by 5.7 % on window TTT, so it is a weak opponent. (4) V149's 'realistic 5-8 % drop' was a max-based statistic on zipper + Krauss at 0.5 s, whose QDF equals SUMO's zipper cap at 0.5 s (already noted in V181 and not acted on) and is step-dependent. The KILL stands; the realism premise does not. (5) The critic's corrections are adopted in this reading: bistability and hysteresis are features of a real drop, so the defects are an unrealistically large (about 42 %), near-deterministic, single fixed drop; no controller has yet been tested on a plant with a verified drop, because no such plant exists in this project.

V25911-02B build, milestone 1 (stages S, C0, ladder) and smoke
full entry
B build, milestone 1 (stages S, C0, ladder) and smoke (V258; commits f3f0c4c, 7da3c02). Built: corridor.build(speed, name) with the m32 net (edges 4 and 5 keep 3 lanes; id loops a_end on 3a and ma_end 300 m into edge 3; ramp32's spec and cached net ramp32_131a87b358 unchanged); fleet.B_ALKS_SHARE (one uniform per vehicle: trucks 7.5 %, then ALKS, so trucks match and ALKS sets nest across shares; v199's draw unchanged when unset) and fleet.ALKS_EXPLICIT; v5b/fleet/b_merge.py (one run: constant demand, id-based merges and crossings, the deadlock detector, NCμ, the hold controls, trip hash, per-vehicle times) and v5b/fleet/b_stage.py (jobs, runner, smoke checks, C0 tables, lattice and step criteria, ladder with extensions, loading, stuck and tool-artefact rules, logistic L1/L2); 6 unit tests; full suite 385 passed. Choices made while building, disclosed: (1) B has its own runner, so day.run_day and its two == corridor.NAME tests are untouched; (2) a merge is a ramp vehicle's first step on 3a off lane 0 (or on edge 3), because a vehicle that enters 3a_0 and changes lane in the same step is never listed on 3a_0 (the first build missed 24 of 258); (3) NCμ takes the first ALKS within 1 m/s of 27.78 m/s that is faster than the cap, so the 1-s cap binds (the first build picked a vehicle below it); (4) the deadlock control 1 locks the held vehicle's lane changes and holds it within the last 5 m of 3a_1, not 10 m: with lane changes allowed the standing vehicle could move off lane 0, and a 9.8-m gap let cars squeeze in ahead and cross (V231 smoke caught this; failed smoke kept as _smoke_f3f0c4c_failed); (5) milestone 1 builds only the no-control stages; the control arms (UGR, OR, shadows, sham, E_MA) are built only if C0 and the ladder leave B testable, and the smoke before stage T covers them. Smoke (frozen 7da3c02, seed 7,431,110, 12 short runs): all checks pass (echoes, counts by id, merges = ramp trips with sub-second times, class shares, ALKS read-back, NCμ binds and changes the trip hash, unset-vType trip hash identical, both deadlock controls, m32 and ramp32 nets). Cost: median 0.0071 wall-s per simulated s (max 0.0131).

V26111-02B C0 result: B-UNTESTABLE(m32, step) by the pre-registered tables; cause is the onset rule, not deadlocks
full entry
B C0 result: B-UNTESTABLE(m32, step) by the pre-registered tables; cause is the onset rule, not deadlocks (frozen 7da3c02, units b-c0-7da3c02 then b-c0b-7da3c02; 180 runs, 0 failed; docs/research/results/b_c0_v0.json; numbers only). Fewer than 9/10 NC runs broke down at 1.10 × B0 for every share, so 1.25 × B0 ran too. No run was evaluable for C0.2 or C0.3 (0 runs with ≥ 10 queued intervals; 0 step pairs), so Lat and St fail at both steps for every share and the table gives B-UNTESTABLE(m32, step). Deadlocks: 0 events in 120 NC runs at both steps (D passes for every share). Merge onsets by the approved rule (all-lane merge_up speed < 13.9 m/s for 4 readings), per 10 runs at 0.1 / 0.05 s: 25 % 0/0 (1.10), 1/0 (1.25); 50 % 2/0, 5/1; 80 % 0/1, 4/1. Yet the merge is loaded: median MA-end flow in 40-70 min against demand at 1.10 × B0 (5,287 veh/h) is 5,197 (25 %), 4,866 (50 %), 4,491 (80 %), and at 1.25 × B0 (6,008) 5,432, 4,883, 4,392; median max insertion backlog 41-617 vehicles at 1.10 and 346-1,505 at 1.25; the lane-0 merge_up speed falls to a median minimum of 0.1-0.8 m/s, while the all-lane minimum stays at 11.4-13.0 m/s. The report-only lane-0 onset fired on 7/10 runs only at 25 %, 1.10, 0.1 s, and on 0/10 elsewhere. Reading (inference): lane 0 stands at the merge, but the vehicle-weighted three-lane speed stays above the threshold, and a 30-s interval in which no vehicle passes the loop reads as free (the residual the draft flagged as report-only, §4). Also, B0 = 3 × 1,602 sits above m32's merge throughput at 50 % and 80 % ALKS (about 4,870 and 4,450 veh/h), so 1.10 and 1.25 × B0 are standing-queue and entry-limited levels there. B stops for the author (any continuation needs a new V decision).

(1) The merge onset uses the approved 4-reading rule (speed < 13.9 m/s on 4 consecutive 30-s readings) on the lane-0 merge_up loop (merge_up_2_0), and an interval in which that loop was occupied but no vehicle passed counts as standing (speed 0), not as free (b_merge.lane0_speed, series field 13); the all-lane reading stays report-only (breakdowns_merge_alllane). (2) Claude's addition, disclosed: a run counts as broken down when a merge episode overlaps the window (onset before 4,200 s and recovery after 600 s), because at overloaded levels the queue forms during the warm-up (a stored 50 % run at 1.10 × B0: one episode 450-4,740 s), which the 'in-window onset' wording would count as no breakdown. (3) Seeds: 7,431,191-200 (grep-clean) replace 7,431,111-120 for C0 and the NC ladder (§7 row C); 111-120 are retired as used. Only no-control data were read before this change.

V26811-02Goal correction: speed and throughput are to be maximised, not only safety proxies
full entry
Goal correction: speed and throughput are to be maximised, not only safety proxies (author, on V267: "we also want to maximize speed and throughput"; asked why 30 km/h). Correction to Claude's wording: '30 km/h cap' in V267 means an offset, a cap of desired speed minus 30 km/h on the 6 nearest mainline ALKS only, about 70 km/h at the 100 km/h limit. The offset list was Claude's arbitrary choice, and 30 was its top. The cap floor is 50 % of desired speed, so offsets above 50 km/h change nothing. Run 2 fixed offsets, same environment (10-s decisions, seeds 7,419,820-839; docs/research/results/b_run2_const*.json; exploratory, no multiplicity control): offset 50 reduces TTC < 3 s by 52 [25, 86] / 44 [22, 82] / 23 [13, 29] % and braking by 39 [32, 47] / 32 [26, 51] / 16 [9, 26] % at 4,090 / 4,300 / 4,600 veh/h. Every offset leaves vehicles in system within -0.2 to +1.0 % and arrivals within 0.5 %. So neither fixed caps nor the current reward target efficiency; mean speed is not measured directly yet. Run 2 keeps running pending the author's choice on the reward.

full entry
Slowing-down bias named as a challenge to address; m32 shows no capacity drop (author: every RL algorithm, in v5 too, learned to slow down instead of keeping high speed and throughput with no collisions and a low capacity drop). Report-only check on the stored ladder and C0 runs (no-control, 0.1 s, onsets after 900 s only; 10-min mean flow before onset vs mean from onset + 5 min, at MA end; no null computed, n = 1-6 per level): at 50 % ALKS, pre / discharge veh/h 4,344 / 4,498 (demand 4,325, n 4), 4,488 / 4,532 (4,566, n 3), 4,662 / 4,663 (4,806, n 2); drop -4.7 / -2.0 / -0.1 %; 25 % and 80 % shares -8.2 to -2.2 %. Discharge is not below pre-onset flow, though that flow is limited by demand, so a drop against a true maximum is not excluded. Correction to V269's reply: the 4-6 % gap at 4,600 veh/h was called the most throughput control could recover; with discharge at or above about 4,500 veh/h much of it may be vehicles stored at lower speed, so that bound is not supported. Run 3 at about a third of training: mean offset about 26-31 → 29-34 km/h (uniform 25), mean speed and flow past the merge flat. Claude's reading, not tested: the actuator can only slow, proxies fall at once with speed, and without a drop holding back cannot add flow. Proposal awaiting the author: a fixed-headway sweep on ALKS tau, a contract change.

I pick B for now"; on C, per-CAV policies: wants to consider it, concerned about competing with large teams). One central PPO policy sets a target headway per zone (upstream, merge area, downstream) every 10 s. The V2V rule applies it: an ALKS behind an ALKS within 150 m, same leader on two 1-s updates, uses its zone's target; otherwise tau 1.6. No speed or lane-change commands. This extends the contract's headway change from the sweeps to training (exploratory), and it knowingly moves B's question from gap creation for merging towards capacity through adaptive headway. Per-CAV control stays open until zones have a result.

Correction: the "short gap" measure counted stopped queues, not risky following; Claude's error; run 5 restarted (found 23:13 while explaining V282's sharp cutoff). In 6 traced runs (delay and no delay, tau 0.8-1.1 s) every follower-second with a bumper gap < 2.5 m was at speed ≤ 1 m/s, resting at 2.30-2.50 m, mostly ALKS behind ALKS on 3a; none was moving. SUMO's minGap is 2.5 m, so a stopped queue sits on the threshold. Seven stored rows re-run with the split (5,300 and 4,600 veh/h, tau 0.8-1.0, delay and no delay, one policy): all other metrics identical, 17-1,628 old gaps, 0 moving. Consequences: (1) the gap numbers in V274, V276, V279, V280 and V282 do not show close following; their "gap" columns measure stopped followers, and all "trade flow for gaps" readings are withdrawn. (2) Run 4's W_GAP penalty charged stopped queues, so its backing off at 5,300 may be caused by this, not a slowing bias. Run 4 must not be read as a test of learning; it was run with a wrong penalty. (3) V282's level list was based on this and on 10 seeds; the 20-seed V280 rows show more flow below 1.2 s with delay (+2.0 / +3.4 / +4.1 % at 1.2 / 1.0 / 0.8 s, 5,300 veh/h), so 1.2 s is not a cutoff. V282's "no more flow" is withdrawn. TTC < 3 s (-31 / -54 / -88 %) remains a real cost. (4) The 420-event contact is unchanged. Fix: gap25 counts only followers above 1 m/s, stop_gap the rest. Run 5 keeps the delay, change cost and references, with the full list 1.6, 1.2, 1.0, 0.8 s; the abandoned attempt stopped at rule tuning, no training. New bar, fixed before data (replaces V281's): at least 2 of 3 final policies, at the same level (4,600 or 5,300), on 7,419,930-949: flow better than delay alone, CI excluding 0; 0 collisions; at most 100 moving short-gap follower-s; and against the tuned rule and each listed fixed arm whose flow is at least the policy's minus 0.5 % (median paired), TTC < 3 s and braking both better, CIs excluding 0. Rule tuning (7,419,950-959): among rules with TTC < 3 s and braking medians at 4,600 and 5,300 no worse than fixed 1.2 s, the highest flow gain summed over those levels. A pass gets a check on 7,419,960-979. Fixed arms: 111, 222, 333, 101, 202, 303, 300, 030, 003. Otherwise C starts.

V28611-03C built: one policy shared by every ALKS, per-vehicle targets; reward corrected after a check against known behaviours; per-vehicle rules added as opponents
full entry
C built: one policy shared by every ALKS, per-vehicle targets; reward corrected after a check against known behaviours; per-vehicle rules added as opponents (V285; author's instruction V281). Each ALKS, every 5 s, picks a target headway from 1.6, 1.2, 1.0, 0.8 s using its own observation (position, lane, speed, leader and follower gaps and closing speeds, whether the leader is an ALKS, its level and hold) plus short broadcasts (speed around it, merge zone speed, nearest vehicle on the acceleration lane, count there). A vehicle's target moves one level at most once per 30 s; the V2V rule is unchanged. The critic also sees network state. PPO with parameter sharing, own loop, 3 learners x 3 envs, training seeds from worker 9 up (7,413,600 on). A vehicle that leaves is cut off and its last value bootstrapped, so leaving neither earns nor costs. Reward per vehicle: shared flow, speed and vehicles in system, half its own speed, half the speed around it (200-m bin), minus 10 per second of its own TTC < 3 s or hard braking, minus 5 for its direct follower's, minus 0.05 per move. Check before training: the first reward ranked no change best at 4,600 and 5,300, which would have taught the policy to do nothing: the shared excess-exposure term was noisy, about -0.2 to -0.8 per decision, and one vehicle barely moves it. Removed; safety is charged per vehicle. After the fix no change ranks below every uniform pattern at all levels (3 seeds, seeds 950-952, exploratory). Smoke: level 0 reproduces the zone env exactly, rate limit holds, a policy drives an evaluation row. New opponents, added before C's data: the same fixed patterns applied per vehicle with C's rate limit (each vehicle ramps toward its zone's level, no learning). On 6 tuning seeds at 5,300 this 303 gave 5 % more flow and 10 % more speed than delay alone with 15 % more TTC < 3 s and 20 % more braking events, more flow than the zone-level 333, which needs validation. Tuned on 7,419,950-959 (9 patterns: merge 1.6 s, upstream and downstream each 1.2, 1.0 or 0.8 s); 101, 202, 303 run on 7,419,930-949. C's bar (V285) now also lists every per-vehicle pattern run on those seeds as an opponent: stricter than V283.

Zone-level 0.8 s everywhere (a333) on the same seeds: 4,600 +2.0/+7.9/-67/-44; 5,300 +4.0/+8.9/-88/-41. So about the same flow and speed at about a fifth of its TTC cost at 5,300. One collision in 180 validation episodes: p303, 4,090, seed 7,419,943, traced: an HDV at 0.26 m/s into a stopped ramp ALKS at 3a_0 287.8 m, 7 m from the lane end, the same place as the run 4b contact. Not a following-distance failure; it still counts. Rate limit on tuning seeds 950-959, 5,300: hold 5 / 15 / 30 / 60 s flow +2.0/+3.9/+5.0/+4.8, TTC -18/-14/-30/-37, braking -17/-38/-27/-24; CIs wide, no clear best. Measured: at 5,300 a longer merge-zone headway lowers TTC without lowering flow, so the flow gain comes from outside the merge zone. Claude's idea that the act of opening a gap on entry is what helps is not supported, because the one-level dip still costs -57. Speculation, untested: zone-level 303 gives less flow (+1.6) because vehicles jump 0.8 to 1.6 s at the boundary; the ramp avoids the jump, and slower vehicles stay longer in the zone so reach longer headways, which would make the rule adapt to congestion by itself. Fresh-seed check, fixed before data, seeds 7,419,960-979, p303 chosen as the best of 9 patterns on tuning seeds by flow at 5,300: at each of 4,600 and 5,300 separately, flow above delay alone with CI excluding 0, TTC and braking both better than a333 with CIs excluding 0, flow no more than 1 % below a333 (median paired), moving short gaps 0; collisions traced and reported. C's first training run collapsed toward 1.6 s and was stopped at about 120 of 380 updates (V286, V287; frozen 51429bc; seeds 7,419,960-979, 20 per cell; docs/research/results/b_night_cav_fresh_rows.jsonl, b_night_c1_C*_updates.jsonl). p303 against delay alone, flow / speed / TTC < 3 s / braking: 4,090 +0.7/+4.0/+36/+17; 4,600 +1.9[+0.8,+2.9]/+6.5/-16[-35,+0]/-23[-36,-7]; 5,300 +4.8[+4.1,+5.7]/+11.2/-14[-22,-3]/-19[-22,-9]. Against a333 (flow, TTC, braking): 4,600 -0.1 / +24[+5,+39] / +5[-3,+19], braking CI includes 0, fail; 5,300 -0.1 / +39[+32,+46] / +16[+10,+20], pass. Moving short gaps 0, collisions 0 in 60 p303 episodes. Same seeds: a333 flow +2.1/+5.0, TTC -63/-75; a303 +1.1/+3.2, TTC -3/+8; rule +0.8/+2.4, TTC -1/+10. 1 collision each for a333, a303 and the rule, untraced. A rule, exploratory, not a thesis claim. It trades more TTC and braking events than delay alone for flow and speed at 4,600 and 5,300, and is better on both at 4,090. C run 1: by about update 60-100 C0 and C1 collapsed (entropy 0.05, 1.6 s for 80-93 % of following time in every zone) while the mean reward fell (-0.27 to -0.34), flow and speed fell below their start (5,300: 2,012 to 1,976, 28,085 to 26,899), TTC and braking fell. C2 kept entropy 1.30 with no trend. So the slow-down failure the author described appeared again, even though the reward ranks no change lowest when applied to everyone. Claude's reading, to be measured next: an independent learner sees only its own marginal effect; a vehicle's short headway costs it TTC and a move charge at once, while the speed gain is spread over everyone. The check in V286 compared whole-fleet patterns, which is the wrong test for a per-vehicle learner. Next: measure the reward by own level per zone under random levels, change the reward until the marginal incentive points the right way, then retrain.

V28911-03Why C collapsed, measured: a vehicle's own headway barely changes its own speed; reward corrected; C run 2 starts
full entry
Why C collapsed, measured: a vehicle's own headway barely changes its own speed; reward corrected; C run 2 starts (V288; seeds 7,419,950-959, 10 per level, each ALKS given one random level for its whole trip, so level is independent of position; a first version with random-walk levels was confounded with position and discarded; docs/research/results/b_night_cav_marginal.py, .txt). 1.6 s against 0.8 s, reward terms per vehicle-second while following an ALKS, 4,600: speed term 0.468 / 0.469 in the merge zone, 0.798 / 0.826 upstream, 0.843 / 0.846 downstream; safety term 0.52 / 0.75, 0.18 / 0.17, 0.10 / 0.06. So in the merge zone a short headway has a strong private cost; outside it the private net gain is 0 to +0.05 at most, smaller than the noise, while the fleet-wide gain of +10 % speed at 5,300 is shared and unrewarded. This supports the reading in V288: the benefit is an externality, the slow-down is what independent learners do with it. Correction: each ALKS also earns 0.4 x its flow contribution (speed / spacing, relative to 0.6 veh/s per lane, capped at 1.5), which pays it directly for what it adds to flow. 0.4 chosen from this table: 1.6 s then pays in the merge zone at 4,600 and 5,300, about a tie at 4,090 where short headway is harmless, and 0.8 s pays outside the merge zone at all levels. Move charge reduced to 0.01; the rate limit prevents chatter. The weight is calibrated to a behaviour Claude already knows is good (p303), so C reproducing p303 would not show learning found it unaided; only beating p303 would be informative. C run 2: same network, PPO and limits, 270 updates, training seeds continue from run 1. The bar stays V285 + V286.

Likely cause, Claude's reading, not separately tested: each vehicle decided every 5 s but can move only once per 30 s, so about 5 of 6 samples had no effect. Run 3 change: a vehicle decides only when its own 30-s clock is due; its reward is the mean over that interval; discount 0.8 per decision (about 150 s), 10 epochs. Network, reward (V289), limits, opponents and bar unchanged. Training seeds restart at the workers' first seeds (run 1 used them; these are not evaluation seeds). Check at 40-60 updates: action probabilities must differ between zones; otherwise stop. p303 robustness, seeds 7,419,980-989, 10 per cell, exploratory, against delay at the same setting, flow / speed / TTC < 3 s / braking; then against a333 at that setting, TTC / braking (flow within -1.1 to +0.7): action step 0.3 s, 4,600 +1.2/+6.5/+19/+6, 5,300 +3.2/+8.2/-57/-28; a333 +20/+13, +29/+17. Correction, Claude's error: the per-vehicle reward never reached training in any C run; explanations in V288-V293 withdrawn; fixed (found 05:36 when run 3 and the attribution run gave identical rows; 3aa49fc checkpoints are byte-identical at update 150). The V286 rewrite of CavEnv._efficiency dropped the call that runs _net_stats. Training has report_net off, so nothing computed the per-vehicle terms: reward sd across vehicles 0.0 and no stats, against 0.20 with report_net on, which is the mode of every check and evaluation. What all C runs really trained on: the shared term only (smoothed flow, mean speed, vehicles in system), a shared collision cost and the move charge. No own speed, no flow contribution, no safety term. Withdrawn: V286's reward as trained and the pre-training check as a statement about training; V288's reading of the collapse; V289's statement that the externality caused it and that the flow term corrected it; V290's run 2 and run 3 descriptions as far as the reward goes; V292's "the change that gave this" and its reasons for run 4; run 4's safety weight (it did nothing: run 4 is just run 3 trained 200 updates further); V293's attribution design (it compared a run with itself). What stands, as measured, on evaluation rows, whose metrics do not use the reward: every p-rule and arm result, p303's fresh-seed check and robustness rows, the collision traces, and the validation rows of C runs 3-5 as results of a shared-reward policy. V289's table stands as a measurement of incentives, not as anything training saw. New reading, Claude's, consistent with the code but not separately tested: run 1 collapsed because the move charge (0.05) was the only signal a vehicle could affect, so never moving won; run 2 (charge 0.01, decisions with no effect) had no signal; run 3 (a decision whenever a move is possible) learned from a shared reward alone. It raises flow and speed, does not slow down, and pays in TTC, which is expected with no safety term. So: C with its intended reward has not been tested. The bar failures of runs 3 and 4 apply to a shared-reward, no-safety C. Fix: _efficiency runs the pass; smoke now checks the reward differs across vehicles in training mode. Short run from 05:40 to 06:00 with the intended reward (flow 0.4, safety 10), about 80 updates; run 3 took longer than that to show results, so only its direction will be readable.

A higher weight removes the flow lead without moving C clearly past p303, so the weight moves C along the rules' trade-off and not beyond it. At 4,600 flow ties p303 in all 9 policies; TTC CI excludes 0 only for F0 (+28 [+4,+51]). Weight 40 raised reversals in H0 (2,366 per run) against F's 792-970 on fresh seeds. B with C's shared reward at 5,300: flow against delay alone +3.2, +3.7, +4.2 (run 5: +0.2 to +1.5); B2 is identical to a333 on all metrics; B0 and B1 flow -0.8 and -0.5, TTC +18 and +12 against a333. B changes targets 8-21 times per run, so PPO recovers a near-constant setting: the run 5 failure was the reward, and B learns no adaptation. Against p303, B has flow -1.0 to 0.0, TTC -56 to -30. Grid: no pattern beat p303 clearly on the test seeds, so it is near the best of the 64 on flow and TTC. A: no new runs; its only action lowers speed. Collisions on these seeds: F, G, B 0; H 1 (H1 at 4,600, not traced); p101 1; r2 1. Limits: no plant here has a capacity drop or a condition changing inside a run; 250-500 updates; seeds used once. Exploratory, no claim.

Author: continue with C if promising, and explore many directions first, exploration then exploitation, on this near-perfect simulator; the author's reading is that the road and vehicle models are well optimised and the DRL poorly designed. Stored runs on seeds 7,419,650-669 (no simulation; 1,500-s window; free-flow 234 s; my arithmetic): 4,600 delay alone / p303 / best C: served 97.4 / 99.4 / about 99.3 %, so flow is capped by demand; vehicles in system 381 / 350 / 347-351 against a free-flow 298. 5,300: served 89.1 / 92.9 / 93.8 %, vehicles in system 528 / 483 / 475-480 against 344, mean speed 17.4 / 19.4 / 19.8 m/s against a 27.8 limit. Free flow is a bound, not a target; the true ceiling is unknown. Design limits of C so far: headway is its only action, a 30-s clock, gamma 0.8 at 5-s steps is about a 25-s horizon. Plan pending the author's approval.

Approved: the per-CAV lane action in batch 1, the delay-and-flow shortlist, seeds 7,419,670-799. Rules, no training: p303L1 and p000L1 move mainline ALKS off lane 0 upstream of the merge; p303L2 off lanes 0-1 in the last 1,500 m. Shortlist at 5,300, against p303, medians: delay or flow better; network TTC and braking no more than 10 % worse; 0 collisions; rank by delay % + flow %; top 3. Merge-lane TTC reported alongside. V31211-03Author: the energy line chases perturbations that create waves.
full entry
Author: the energy line chases perturbations that create waves. Real plants are not perfect: what if X perturbs the plant and creates waves, where vehicles must brake and accelerate, which costs fuel or energy? How can DRL mitigate it, and are rule-based, MPC or other neural controllers better? The author agrees equal speed is optimal on an undisturbed plant, at 90 or 100 km/h. Claude's proposal, awaiting the author's pick: first a wave check with no control and a no-X null, then an oracle gap, then a map of X against controller classes.

full entry
Author: adjust the plant so that no control is the best option possible: well calibrated and configured, a reasonably minimal capacity drop, no collisions, no emergency brakes, no teleports, the best fuel, TTC and TTT; this needs many sweeps. Fixed before data, frozen 2b865a1, only no-control runs scored, so no controller result shapes the plant. Unchanged: fleet shares, demand pattern, ALKS tau 1.6 s and 0.5-s delay. Settings: lane changing (lcStrategic, lcCooperative, lcSpeedGain, lcKeepRight, lcAssertive, lcLookaheadLeft, lcSpeedGainLookahead, lcImpatience); road (limit 80-120 km/h, acceleration lane 200-600 m); human drivers (tau scale 0.7-1.0, action step scale 0.25-1.0, sigma scale 0.25-1.0, accel 2.0-3.2, Krauss, IDM or EIDM). These goals conflict, so score = mean over 4,600 and 5,300 and over flow, TTT, fuel per km, network TTC, network braking at 3 m/s² and at 4.5 m/s², of the median paired % improvement on m32, each clipped at 30; equal weights are Claude's choice. Stages: A each value alone, 7,419,610-614; B 100 random combinations in each family (lane changing; plus road; plus drivers), only values that improved in A, 615-617; C top 5 per family with 0 collisions, 618-622; D each family's winner and m32 on 4,090, 4,600, 5,300, 6,000, 623-639. Seeds from V302's unused range. The author picks from D, then the plant is frozen and checked on 640-649, with a new baseline; one tuning pass. Capacity drop reported at D with V271's estimator. Fuel from SUMO's HBEFA4 models, sampled each second. Guard at 95 %.

V32411-03Plant follow-up (V323): lcAssertive works, and a simulator artefact was found.
full entry
Plant follow-up (V323): lcAssertive works, and a simulator artefact was found. 612 runs, 0 failed, seeds 7,419,623-639, docs/research/plant_v1/followup_table.csv; all candidates 0 collisions, 0 teleports; all but all improve ramp delay. At 5,300, r1m3 as adopted / lcAssertive 1.4 / all#96: flow 1,990 / 2,114 / 2,132; vehicles in system 530 / 482 / 470; delay 144 / 111 / 102 s; ramp delay 185 / 61 / 62 s; fuel 86.8 / 82.4 / 82.4 g/km; network TTC 1,990 / 697 / 321; braking at 4.5 m/s² 454 / 197 / 23; braking at 3 m/s² 5,021 / 6,920 / 7,504. Artefact, traced because TTC fell while braking rose: most braking at 3 m/s² is ALKS, at long headway (median about 3.6 s), mostly not closing on the leader, spread along edge 1; traced vehicles in lane 0 run a sawtooth, -4.5 m/s² about every 4 s with the leader 140 m ahead. One seed at 5,300 with lcOvertakeRight 1: ALKS events 3,156 to 908 on r1m3 as adopted, 5,536 to 865 with lcAssertive 1.4; events at headway over 3 s 2,217 to 377 and 4,075 to 330; fuel 86.5 to 81.9 g/km with no other change. So the no-right-overtaking logic is the likely cause, not yet read in the SUMO source; the ALKS 0.5-s action step worsens it (1,540 events at 0.1 s, flow also lower). With lcAssertive 1.4, allowing right overtaking raised network TTC from 104 to 1,745 on that seed, unexplained. lcOvertakeRight was not in the sweep. Every stored braking and fuel count, baseline v0 included, contains this artefact, and a controller could have gained by avoiding it. No plant is frozen; author's decision pending.
