Author: apply the smooth no-undertaking rule, and sweep human undertaking at 0 and 0.5. Part of the ALKS model, so part of the plant, disclosed as our model: SUMO's abrupt rule off for ALKS only; above 60 km/h, not on the acceleration lane, the desired speed is capped at that of a slower vehicle ahead in the left lane within 5 s, by at most a ratio of 1.1 per second, because IDM brakes hard above its desired speed (the first version gave more braking at 7 m/s²). Source check: SUMO's avoidOvertakeRight and canOvertakeRight limit the speed behind the left-lane leader in LC2013. Frozen 124b930; default plant reproduces its stored row. One seed at 5,300, r1m3 as adopted / rule only / rule with lcAssertive 1.4: flow 1,983 / 1,994 / 2,088, fuel 86.5 / 81.1 / 78.1 g/km, braking at 3 m/s² 5,090 / 2,921 / 1,987, free-road ALKS braking 1,866 / 364 / 183, braking at 7 m/s² 5 / 4 / 7. Counter null: passes on the right per run, ALKS allowed to undertake 887, SUMO's rule 80, smooth rule 43-89. Sweep: 13 settings (lcAssertive default, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5 and all#96, each with the rule at human undertaking 0 and 0.5; references r1m3, lcAssertive 1.4, all#96), 4 levels, seeds 7,419,623-639, 884 runs. V34111-04Entry collision explained; wave check protocol fixed before data.
full entry
Entry collision explained; wave check protocol fixed before data. Trace on the one P0 no-control collision (7,419,713, 4,600): a human car inserted at 28 m/s on lane 0 brakes at 4.5 m/s² behind no leader, under SUMO's no-undertaking rule, because lane 1 beside it moves at about 15 m/s; it then cuts into lane 1 with a 0.6-m gap and hits an ALKS 80 m from the entry. With lcAssertive 1.0 on that seed there is none. Rate: P0 1 in 208 no-control runs, the earlier plant 1 in 176, too few to separate. Claude's reading: an insertion effect 3.4 km upstream of the merge; P0 stays frozen and this is disclosed. Wave check, frozen 95af093, r1m3 P0, seeds 7,419,740-749, levels 3,500, 4,090, 4,600 (5,300 has a standing queue that would hide waves). X, each with 3 sizes: brake (a human car near the middle of edge 4 slows to 60, 40, 20 km/h, holds 5 s, every 180 s from 420 s); truck (a truck entering edge 1 capped at 70, 60, 50 km/h, every 300 s from 360 s); burst (ramp departures grouped on a 60, 90, 120-s grid); slow (edge 4 limit 60, 40, 25 km/h for 120 s at 600 and 1,200 s); outage (V2V lost for 15, 30, 60 s at 600 and 1,200 s, against p333, because no control has no V2V headway). Pairs: the same seed without X; no-X rows none and p333. Placebo as the null: a car slows by 5 % for 1 s, every 180 s. 540 runs. A wave: a cell (10 s, 100 m along the mainline) is dipped when mean speed is at least 30 % below its pair; reach is the upstream travel of a connected group of at least 3 dipped cells; wave if median reach is at least 500 m and above the placebo's 95th percentile at that level. With cost: fleet fuel per km at least 3 % worse, CI excluding 0. Thresholds as proposed in V312. Only X that form waves go forward; which, and which controllers, is the author's choice. No controller training in this step.

Oracle test: no speed-cap headroom on the slowdown; a KILL for this kind of action on this X, as fixed in V343. 600 runs, 0 failed, seeds 7,419,790-799, docs/research/phase2/oracle_table.csv. Against p333 under the same X, the best oracle of the 6 is always the mildest (500 m, 80 km/h): delay -0.8 to -2.4 %, worse or tied; fuel -0.1 to +0.2 %; it recovers at most 3 % of its own delay loss; wider or lower caps cost more (at 4,600 slow25 81-92 s against 81 s). 0 of 8 best cases show headroom. Reading: under a capacity loss, flow is unchanged and caps only move the delay; this grid is crude, so it rules out this action, not all smoothing. Resilience, 4,600, slow25, own loss against no X: no control delay -67, fuel -4.7, network TTC -47, braking -37, hard braking -334; p333 delay -73, fuel -4.3, TTC -363, braking -50, hard braking -424. p333 stays ahead on delay under X (+27 %) but its TTC and hard braking are far worse than no control under X (-431 and -27 %). So fixed 0.8 s is good on undisturbed traffic and costly on safety near a disturbance, the first sign that the best headway differs by condition. Untested. Next step is the author's choice.

Hidden driver types: no value; option A is dead in this form, as fixed in V352. 400 runs, 0 failed, seeds 7,419,770-779, docs/research/phase2/type_table.csv, type_rows.jsonl.gz. No variant passes the V346 rule against p333 in any of the 4 conditions, so no hidden-value case. Best hidden variant, tau, at 5,300 without X: delay -3.7 %, network TTC +35 [-42,+140]; with the slowdown at 4,600: delay -3.1 %, TTC +21 [-39,+41]. Why, measured: under p333 at 5,300, 77 % of TTC-seconds have an ALKS as the follower (51 % of exposure), and human rates are flat across the bands of tau (0.06-0.07 per 1,000 vehicle-seconds, 0.19 in the lowest band with 2 % of exposure) and sigma (0.06-0.09). Only very slow drivers stand out (speed factor 0.6-0.7: 0.75, 0.4 % of exposure). So human type barely decides who is in a close approach; the ALKS's own closing does. Also seen, not in the rule: at 4,600 with the slowdown the local rule gives TTC 56 vs 111 with 1 collision in 10 runs; at 5,300 it does not help (with X 226 vs 174, without X 140 vs 57, CIs very wide), so its match holds at 4,090 and 4,600 only. Confirmatory 2 result: per-CAV DRL wins 1 of 20 cells, on safety, on r2m3 under the slowdown at 5,300; it ties everywhere else. Protocol docs/research/protocols/confirmatory_2.md, 2,400 rows, 0 failed, seeds 7,440,100-119, no guard pauses, docs/research/phase3/decide_table.csv, decide_output.txt, eval_rows.jsonl.gz, policies alongside. The won cell, r2m3 X1 5,300, against p333, Bonferroni CI: d0, d1, d2 network TTC +34.5 [+23,+46], +45.0 [+33,+52], +31.1 [+17,+43] (3,560 to 2,294, 1,942, 2,306); braking +15.0, +21.5, +13.6; flow +1.2, +1.0, +1.0; delay +5.3, +0.6, +4.9, CIs including 0; fuel +1.8, +1.5, +1.2; 0 collisions. No delay win in any cell. Near miss: r2m3 X2 5,300, 1 of 3 policies. Elsewhere delay -3.5 to +3.5 % and TTC mixed, including held-out H1 and H2, no cell lost by a clear margin. Allowed sentence: DRL has a conditional advantage in the listed cell; everywhere else as the map shows. Adaptive rule against p333, Bonferroni over 8: wins r1m3 X1 at 4,600 (TTC 58 vs 128) and 5,300 (114 vs 327); does not win X2 (slowdown on edge 3, by merge 1) or on r2m3 (X1 5,300: 2,913 vs 3,560, +11.8), so it is narrower than V351 suggested. Collisions: no control 2 of 400, p333 3 of 400, rule 1 of 400, DRL 1 of 1,200 runs. Traced, one seed: TTC in that cell is mostly on 4a (1,858 of 3,461 for p333) at median speed 5-7 m/s, a real close-following queue at merge 2 next to the slowdown. The policies hold about level 1.1-2.0 on 4a in calm and event periods alike, against 3 elsewhere: mostly a position pattern, not a reaction to the event. So a fixed rule with a longer headway on 4a may match it; this was not among the opponents and must be checked before this win means learning was needed. Limits: the protocol was not adversarially reviewed; rules had no tuning on r2m3 while DRL trained on this family; network TTC is heavy-tailed; 20 seeds.

V36711-04Review of the handoff page against code and history: the page matches its sources, but the review found that P0 hides full 9 m/s² ALKS braking from every 1-Hz metric, so ...
full entry
Review of the handoff page against code and history: the page matches its sources, but the review found that P0 hides full 9 m/s² ALKS braking from every 1-Hz metric, so the sawtooth was not removed, it changed form. No new seeds; no controller; docs/research/p0_trace/. Traced at 0.1 s, seeds 7,419,640 and 641 at 5,300, earlier plant vs P0: ALKS braking at 7 m/s² and harder 3 and 3 vs 1,749 and 972 vehicle-s (2,149 at 4,600, seed 640), of which the stored metric sees 0, 0 and 4; at 4.5 m/s² 342 and 371 vs 2,451 and 1,307, while the metric reads 361 and 359 vs 146 and 50; free-road ALKS braking at 3 m/s² 1,715 and 1,940 vs 2,261 and 1,342, while the metric reads 1,743 and 1,916 vs 246 and 185. Full-emergency events per run 24 and 29, all at the lane end, vs 2,744 and 1,507 (3,673 at 4,600), 99 % on a capped ALKS, each losing about 4.5 m/s. Flow and human braking do improve: flow 2,039 and 1,937 vs 2,123 and 2,101; humans at 4.5 m/s² 145 and 190 vs 33 and 16. The instrumented runs reproduce the stored flow. Mechanism, one ALKS alone on an empty road: lowering maxSpeed makes SUMO's IDM aim at the cap within one 0.1-s step (MSCFModel_IDM::freeSpeed, seen < secGap), and the 0.5-s action step holds that deceleration for 0.5 s: cap ratio 1.02 gives -5.45 m/s², 1.1 gives -9, speed undershoots the cap. The rule updates on the whole second, the braking ends before the next whole second, and metrics sample on the whole second: sampled at phase 0.5 instead of 0.0 the 7 m/s² count on seed 640 is 3,494, not 0; the earlier plant is flat across phases. Near the rule's 60 km/h threshold this forms a cycle of about 3 s, for example 13.4 to 18 m/s. Claude's errors: the ratio 1.1 of V326 did not remove the braking, it moved it out of the sample; the comment at b_env.py:74 is wrong, and section 4b repeats it in two charts; section 4b's Euler line is wrong, SUMO switches to ballistic because of the action step. What this changes: the braking, free-road and sawtooth statements of V324, V327, V329 and baseline v1 do not hold as measured, and the author's pick in V328 used them. V314's no-emergency-braking target is not met. Flow, delay and collisions are outcomes of the plant as built and stand for that plant, but it is not the clean plant the records describe. TTC, fuel and jerk use the same 1-Hz sample and are not tested for this. The reward's braking term has the same blind spot. Speed-cap results (V339, V344) used this actuator and need a look. Verification otherwise: 365 V rows present, 12 update rows missing and 3 rows cut at a table bar; paths, commit hashes, tags and code names exist, except files the shot has not written; decide_table, rulecheck_table and baseline check_table regenerate byte-identically; the page's reproduce command and a P0 row reproduce exactly; metrics, observation and reward as written match the code. Validation: a cold reader with only the page answered 14 of 16; it missed the free seeds and the 7 candidate problems, which are only in chart labels. Page not changed by this review. (update) Correction, Claude's checker: the 3 rows reported as cut at a table bar (V196, V231, V236) are complete on the page; the checker stripped <...> from the log's text. The 12 (update) rows are the real omission.

The fix and its check, fixed before data. Fix, ease flag (frozen below): the smooth rule's target is still set on the whole second, but each ALKS's cap moves toward it every 0.1 s, staying a small step under its speed, so the ratio of 1.1 per second written in V326 finally holds. One vehicle: minimum acceleration -2.53 m/s² against -9 as built. The plant is called P0c, docs/research/p0c/plant_p0c.json; P0 still reproduces under its old settings. New metrics, every step: braking, ALKS full-emergency events, free-road braking, fuel, jerk; TTC also at the half second; passes on the right split by kind. Development runs, used seeds 7,419,640-641, not a check: full-emergency events earlier plant 24, 29, P0 2,744, 1,507, P0c 21, 3; free-road braking 1,715, 1,940, 2,261, 1,342, 217, 146; 1-Hz TTC and fuel agree with the half-second TTC and step fuel on all three plants, so those two were not biased by V367. Review of confirmatory 3: 65 findings and 11 from a final critic; 64 confirmed by a skeptic; revision 1 should not run as written, and revision 2 awaits the author. 11 agents, about 2.5 million tokens, far above Claude's earlier estimate of 100,000 for one reviewer. docs/research/protocols/confirmatory_3_review.md. No new seeds; 4 single runs on used seed 7,419,640, docs/research/p0_trace/review3/. Main findings. (1) A second hidden braking source: when an ALKS loses V2V, _v2v sets tau from 0.8 to 1.6 s at once (b_env.py, want = ... ALKS_TAU0). r2m3 P0d, 5,300, one seed, p333 X1 and X2: braking at 7 m/s² 71.3 and 75.3 vehicle-s against 1-Hz 11 and 5; full-emergency events 112 and 106, 67 and 74 of them moving, against no control's 15 and 19, all creep at a lane end. About 13-41 times smaller than V367, and step counters see it. No policy was traced. (2) The slowdown taper steps once per second: step against 1-Hz braking within the taper 345 / 93 and 411 / 95 in X1, about 1 % of TTC. (3) Network TTC is mostly a low-speed queue: p333, one seed, median follower speed 5.0 and 7.4 m/s, 48-62 % below 7 m/s, 61-79 % of records with a leader stopped on 4a or ramp 2; median needed deceleration about 0.8-1.0 m/s². It is also a reward term, and most of it falls after the slowdown. (4) The 30 % bar against a tuned rule: estimated any-cell pass about 5-20 % at the effect sizes seen, from P0 rows; no-effect false positives 0 of 3,000. (5) One opponent picked on 20 seeds is mostly noise; no rule reads own speed; delay over finishers can flip the 2 % gate; no closure on a loss; the claim-deciding code does not exist and had no review step; c_train can silently run P0c or r1m3; no check under a controller. Not confirmed: 1 finding. Claude confirmed (1) in the code and the stored traces. Revision 2 adopts most of it, and the author decides: tau and taper changes, the claim bar, closing the line, code review, CPU limit, seeds 7,440,065-074.

V38111-05Code review of confirmatory 3, 3 agents, about 720,000 tokens; no result would have changed on a clean run, but the chain could not have started, and failures would have ...
full entry
Code review of confirmatory 3, 3 agents, about 720,000 tokens; no result would have changed on a clean run, but the chain could not have started, and failures would have hung or misread; all fixed. Simulation code: no blocker or major defect; old rows reproduce with the new flags off (73 keys identical), and the actuators do what they should. Claim code: thresholds, signs and seeds match the protocol; fixed: thresholds read rounded numbers; the safety word counted apart from the winners; the table's collisions were a median; no adaptation gain; no completeness check; missing metrics read as 0. Run chain: fixed: the training smoke would always fail (it read tau every 5 s against a limit per second); one failed job silently ran out the batch; a dead environment worker hung the learner forever (b.close()); a restart corrupted the collapse check; a crash was noticed only hours later; re-running retrained everything; the saved settings were never checked; no watchdog; pre-run checks not enforced by the chain (now prerun_all.sh writes the marker chain.sh requires). Tests: 34 of 35 deliberately wrong versions passed before, 0 of 40 now; 69 tests. Open for the author, defaults in the code, nothing run on them yet: (1) tau gate: eligible ALKS on the commanded level at least 98 % of the time, because equality cannot hold under the rate limit; (2) rules answer every 5 s and policies every 10 s, both at most one level per 10 s: kept and disclosed, which favours the rules; (3) the copy rule always runs on evaluation seeds, deciding only if it meets the delay filter; (4) a delay win counts as a win for closing the line; (5) replication uses this protocol's limits, not V359's older counters; (6) "no worse" on severe samples is a paired median at or below 0; (7) the sentence's figure is the range over the 5 policies against the counting rule with the lowest TTC; (8) adaptation gain: the counting rule with the lowest TTC against the single rule, and the share DRL closes, reported only if that gap's CI excludes 0; (9) the 2-seed trace is replaced by counters by road, speed and period on all 20 evaluation seeds.

Author asked whether the inputs are well normalised. Measured: no. They are scaled by hand, not normalised, and input [11] is dead; no effect on confirmatory 3's validity, to be disclosed with its result. 69,579 greedy decisions, stored policy C1, S and X1 at 5,300, used seed 7,419,640; teaching trace, not a result. c_train.py has no running mean-and-spread layer. Dead: hold left is exactly 0 at every decision, because a vehicle is asked only when its 10-s clock is due and moves at most once per 10 s, so true since V290; its 64 actor weights moved exactly 0 from the seed-rebuilt start over 500 updates, as did its critic weights, which also confirms that rebuild. The policy has 15 working inputs. Spread: x/1000 has SD 1.90; most others 0.1 to 0.3 with means of 0.2 to 0.8. Saturated: x/300 at a limit in 93 % of decisions, nearest accel-lane vehicle in 84 %. x/300 centres on merge 1 only, so merge 2 has only the coarse x/1000 for position, plus inputs [14] and [15]. Effect on learning: not measured. The frozen run continues unchanged (fae4620, V383): 0 × weight adds nothing to any decision, and the scaling is the same for all 5 policies. If the DRL line closes, these belong in the limits: the result is for this input design, not for per-CAV DRL in general. Page: scaling table in section 3; input [11] locked in the live network.

Kept, not read: rule tuning (2,800 rows), no-control rows, first selection, since rules do not use policy inputs. Design: inputs of actor and critic scaled by running mean and SD, clip 5, saved in the checkpoint; one pilot collection before update 0 for the first statistics, nothing learned from it; statistics move only between updates, so the probability ratio holds; policies from before this change act exactly as before. Smoke in training mode, 3 updates: probability ratio at the start of each update within 4e-7 of 1; statistics fixed during updates; scaled inputs centred; per-vehicle reward varies (SD 0.35-0.76); explained variance -0.04, 0.33, 0.47; KL 0.004-0.008. Claude's smoke tolerance was too tight: in one batch input [15] had scaled mean -0.55 and SD 0.28 against the running statistics, a batch-to-batch shift; tolerance widened after seeing it, a smoke criterion, not a protocol gate. Training cannot be widened without changing the protocol (5 learners x 3 environments): 23-24 s per update, CPU 38 %. So the evaluation rows that do not depend on the policies (no control, p333, the chosen rules, the single rule; 1,000 of about 1,850 runs) run now on 16 workers, from frozen d2b2ecc, with precompute_eval.py. It uses the same names, configs and files as eval_runs.py, so the chain's evaluation step skips them. Rows are not read before the chain's reading. An arm the final selection drops stays complete and unused: the reading takes names from opponents.json, and check_rows requires complete arms only. Guard raised to 95 % for both units. CPU 83-87 %, package 88 °C.

V39211-05The precompute of V391 is stopped: it slowed training from about 23.5 to 40-45 s per update, cancelling its gain.
full entry
The precompute of V391 is stopped: it slowed training from about 23.5 to 40-45 s per update, cancelling its gain. With 16 extra workers CPU was 83-87 % and the package 88 °C. Renicing them to 19 still left training at about 40 s, so the cause is likely contention on shared cores and heat rather than scheduling priority. Not measured further. Training is the long pole and cannot be widened under the protocol, so nothing runs beside it. The 92 rows done are moved to eval_primary.precomputed_unused.jsonl and not used; the chain's evaluation starts from clean files, as designed. Training back to 23-24 s per update. Cost: about 10 minutes. Expected end about 17:00: training about 15:10, tracing and copy rule about 15:25, evaluation about 80 minutes at 24 workers. The guard stays at 95 %.

Author: both, TensorBoard and the curves on the DRL page; "Be very careful how you update the metrics. In the past, I've done some mistakes that tricked me." Done after training ended at 15:10; the chain's collapse check passed and it went on to tracing. TensorBoard 2.21.0 in its own environment, venv_tb, so the chain's environment was not touched mid-run; pins in toolchain/requirements_tb_lock.txt. One source for both views: trainlog.py checks the logs, then derives the series (conf3/trainlog.json, copy beside the page). Checks: every update once, no crashed attempts, every seed as expected, one episode per demand level, constant critic scale, no missing values, network counts absent as designed; shown to fire first on 4 planted faults, all caught. to_tensorboard.py writes and reads back 119,995 values, 0 mismatches; trainlog_independent.py recomputes 30,210 values from the raw logs with its own slowdown draw, 0 mismatches. Every tag carries its definition and limits. Training episodes are labelled with their slowdown, recomputed from the seed, and traffic is shown split by it. Claude's errors found by these checks or by looking: a wrong seed expectation, a TensorFlow-only writer call, float64 values that TensorBoard's default loader drops without a warning (rewritten as float32; served values within 6e-8), a KL axis that rounded to 0.00, and percentages on TTC counts of 12-74. TensorBoard runs on 127.0.0.1:6006, unit tb-conf3. Training curves are not the result.

full entry
Confirmatory 3, revision 4, fixed reading: primary cell X2 is won on TTC by the tuned reading; X1 is not, and closes by [A3]. Verification before any thesis use is pending. Chain done 16:36, every step rc=0, no tracebacks, collapse check passed, every arm complete on 20 evaluation seeds; conf3/decide3_table.csv, decide3_map.csv, chain.log. X2 (edge 3, 30 km/h, 180 s, 5,300): counting rules p333, r4a1, lr1000_16_2, os1_15_10; a4400_10_1 excluded by the delay filter. 4 of 5 policies clear every limit against every counting rule. TTC against the lowest-TTC counting rule, os1_15_10: +24.0 [12.2, 30.1], +30.0 [21.0, 40.7], +8.5 [-0.6, 32.0] (d2 fails), +27.3 [17.7, 34.9], +25.0 [20.7, 35.1] %. Replication against p333: 5 of 5. Delay win: 1 of 5, no. The protocol allows the word "safety" in X2: 4 winning policies are no worse than every counting rule on samples at 3 m/s² or more. The copy rule did not meet the delay filter: median TTC 1,758 and delay 254,611 veh-s, against p333's 2,516 and 238,734. The single rule lr400_13_2 is cleared by 4 of 5. Medians for no control: TTC 1,639, delay 297,046 veh-s, braking 3,497; 1 of 5 policies worse than it on TTC. Where the gain is: roads 3 and 4a and the second ramp, all speed bands, mostly outside the slowdown periods. X1 (edge 4, 25 km/h): only p333 counted; 3 of 5 clear, since d2 and d3 exceed the 2 % delay limit. TTC against p333 +33.2 to +46.2 %, CIs excluding 0; replication 3 of 5, not met; single rule cleared by 5 of 5. All 5 policies are worse than no control on TTC: no control had fewer such seconds, at 37.5 % more delay. Map: no harm cells. Collisions 0 in every primary arm. Claude's reading of the medians, not a protocol test: the policies' TTC is lower than p333's in most map cells, steady traffic included, at about equal delay, so the edge seems not specific to slowdowns. Check: the tuned verdicts were recomputed from the raw rows with separate code and its own resampling: X2 4 of 5, X1 3 of 5, the same policies failing for the same reasons. Allowed sentence, X2: "In an uncalibrated SUMO model of a three-lane freeway with two on-ramps 1.2 km apart and 50 % automated vehicles, at 5,300 veh/h, with ideal V2V and ideal roadside speeds: under a tapered slowdown to 30 km/h for 180 s on the road between the ramps, at least 4 of 5 per-CAV PPO headway policies had fewer seconds at TTC below 3 s than each of 4 counting rules tuned on separate seeds, 8.5-30.0 % over the 5 policies against the counting rule with the lowest TTC, with delay and flow within the stated limits. This is a surrogate."

full entry
Verification of V395 (author switched to Extra High with ultracode): the fixed verdict stands, X2 won and X1 closed, but the claim is narrower than V395 suggested, and 3 of Claude's statements are withdrawn. 15 agents, about 2.56 M tokens, read-only; docs/research/conf3/verification_rev4.md and digest. Clean: provenance, arithmetic, selection, no artefact or shifted cost against the counting rules. Narrower: the X2 gain arises after the slowdown, in the recovery queue (82-96 % in 1,000-1,800 s), mostly at merge 2 (4a and ramp 2) and on road 3. The policies are not below no control on TTC below 3 s (-14.8 to +2.9 %), and ALKS braking at 3 m/s² is 9-18 % above no control; "safety" means against the tuned 0.8-s rules only. The cell was won at the minimum, 4 of 5; full seed bootstrap gives "won" about 27-30 % of the time, mostly from the point-median delay and flow limits. The win depends on the filter excluding a4400_10_1 (with it, 3 of 5). Off merge 2 the gain against lr1000_16_2 is below the margin, and merge-2 lane-end behaviour was never validated. X1's closure is equally knife-edge, so no X2-versus-X1 reading. Withdrawn, Claude's errors: "mostly outside the slowdown periods" (period bins use absolute time after a 300-s warm-up); "the edge seems not specific to slowdowns"; the copy rule's "about 7 %" delay (8.6 % on the protocol statistic). Also corrected: the aborted run did 5 updates, not 3 (V388); V395's separate-code recheck ran inline and was not kept. Completed X2 sentence and the X1 reading in the verification file. Protocol: dated addendum of factual corrections, no claim rule changed. Open, needing SUMO and the author: a determinism replay of one policy arm, merge-2 per-lane TTC with the follower-class split, a longer window; and whether rule-only opponents suffice for a thesis claim (V95). A verification agent left a 38 MB fae4620.tar in the repo; moved to scratch, never committed.

full entry
The open replays of V396 are done (report-only, cannot change the verdict). Determinism holds; the X2 TTC edge survives a longer window and is not only lane-end creep; human drivers gain too. Merge-2 lanes still carry a shift against r4a1. docs/research/conf3/rerun/analysis.txt; 400 runs, frozen d2b2ecc, evaluation seeds, finished 18:31. Reproduction: all 200 base replays reproduce every stored number (28,555 keys); all 200 long runs equal the stored deciding count at 1,800 s. Paired statistic over the reference median, 97.5 % bootstrap, policies d0-d4. Longer window (to 3,000 s): TTC below 3 s over 300-3,000 s is lower than every counting rule for all 5 policies, CIs excluding 0: against os1_15_10 +18.3 to +38.0 %, lr1000_16_2 +24.0 to +40.5 %. In 1,800-3,000 s alone: +27.0 to +43.4 % against os1_15_10. Whole-run delay: equal or better (d1 +14.2 [2.8, 21.4] %); flow +0.2 to +0.6 %. The queue never clears at 5,300 in any arm (last 10 minutes 80-82 veh/min, backlog at 1,800 s 430-530). Against no control, TTC still equal (-18.9 to +4.1 %, CIs spanning 0), delay 33-38 % better. Merge 2 by lane: excluding the accelerating lane 4a_0, the gain against os1_15_10 stays at +15.9 to +29.9 % (4 of 5 CIs above 0); against lr1000_16_2 +10.4 to +31.5 %. In 4a_0's last 50 m: 47-63 % fewer than os1_15_10. On the 4a mainline lanes, policies have more TTC than r4a1 (d0 -45.7 [-65.5, -13.7] %) and far more than no control: part of the gain is moved from the accelerating lane to the mainline. Who gains: ALKS followers +16.6 to +35.5 % against os1_15_10, but above no control (-13 to -42 %). Human and truck followers +4.2 to +17.0 % against os1_15_10 (4 of 5 CIs above 0) and +9.3 to +20.9 % against no control. Humans behind humans, a pair no reward term charges, +6.3 to +16.9 % against os1_15_10 (1 of 5 CIs above 0) and +8.1 to +23.4 % against p333 (4 of 5). So no shift to human drivers; the policies' total near no control comes from fewer human-follower conflicts and more ALKS-follower ones. ALKS followers hold 58-66 % of TTC seconds. Limits: same evaluation seeds, longitudinal TTC only, report-only. Still open: the thesis-scope question (V95).

4. Networks to scale

Point 0 is the start of edge 3a, where the code's _x has 0. Every x below is computed by script from the lane lengths in net.xml, in metres. Horizontal is to scale. Vertical is schematic: lane width and ramp offset are exaggerated.

Three coordinates differ by a few metres. (1) x, used here: lane lengths summed from 3a, junctions not counted. (2) Node coordinates from the node file: 3a is 300 m between nodes but 294.72 m of lane, because the junctions take the rest. (3) Road distance adds SUMO's internal junction lanes: 2.98 m between edges 2 and 3a, 9.82 m from rj into 3a, 8.00 m between 3a and 3, 0.10 m at most others. So a vehicle drives about 11 m more than x says from edge 2 to edge 3. The code ignores this: a vehicle inside a junction keeps its last _x (b_env.py). Your expected r1m3 and r2m3 values match the net files. Measured

The policy's reward zones stay 3 on r2m3: on r2m3 _zone treats 4a, 4 and 5 as down.

Code constants on r2m3. _x uses LEN_3 = 1196 and LEN_4 = 1000, but on r2m3 those lanes are 1,194.3 and 996.0 m. So the policy's position input is +1.7 m too high from 4a on and +5.7 m on edge 5, and it clips at 3,000 m, so the last 280 m read the same. Small, but a new agent should know. ROAD_X and ZonePattern.X use the same offsets. Open whether it matters; I expect not.

4b. Current plant: every setting

What "current" means. Two plants with the same settings: r1m3 P0, frozen as baseline v1 (V329), and r2m3, the same drivers and rules with a second ramp (V354), on which confirmatory 2 and the DRL shot ran. Both hide hard braking (V367). This section gives those settings. The accepted plant is P0d, baseline v2 (V376): the rule's cap moves every 0.1 s, it looks 8 s ahead instead of 5, and it may brake up to 4.4 m/s² when needed. The second hidden source under controllers, the V2V headway rise, and the 1-s taper are fixed for confirmatory 3 by two further settings, docs/research/conf3/plant_c3.json (V382). Point 0 is the start of 3a. Nothing here is a claim about real traffic.

Values were read back from SUMO 1.27.1 on seed 7,419,640 (r1m3 baseline check seed, no traffic result read; 3 simulated seconds each plant). Distributions: 40 seeds drawn from fleet.py at 5,300 veh/h, 106,128 vehicles, no simulation. Measured

Car following

ALKS: IDM

accel = 2.6 x [1 - (v / v_des)4 - (s* / gap)2]

s* = 2.5 + v x tau + v x (v - v_lead) / (2 x sqrt(2.6 x 4.5))

From MSCFModel_IDM.cpp, SUMO 1.27.1. No noise.

Humans and trucks: Krauss

Drive at the speed that stays safe if the leader brakes, within tau, then randomly slower, scaled by sigma.

The smooth no-undertaking rule (P0 change 2)

P0, cap every 1 sP0c, cap every 0.1 sTarget

Both charts are measured on a bench. A lowered cap is reached within one 0.1-s step and the 0.5-s action step holds that braking, so a ratio of 1.1 on a once-per-second cap gives 9 m/s², not the 1.2 m/s² this page first said. The first version without the limit caused 7 m/s² braking (V326). The rule covers all ALKS, on main road and ramps. Measured

In and out of the plant

Not in this plant

✗ Off-ramps. Vehicles leave only at the end of edge 5

✗ Grades, curves. All nodes on a straight line; ramp offset is geometry only

✗ Truck lane rules. Trucks enter any lane and may use any lane

✗ Weather. Fixed to dry: factors 1.0, 1.0

✗ Crashes, stalled vehicles. No crash process in this environment; the v199 factor 3.0 stays inert

✗ Teleporting. Off: time-to-teleport -1

✗ ACC or CACC vehicles. 0 %; the classes exist in the code but are not drawn

✗ Changing demand. Constant rate per run, no peak shape

✗ Meter action. Signal node rm stays green under no control

✗ Signal on ramp 2. Node rm2 on r2m3 is a priority node, so no meter can act there as built

✗ Detectors on ramp 2 and 4a. r2m3 reuses r1m3's loop list; r2, rj2 and 4a have none

✗ Sublane movement. lateral-resolution off, lane changes take no time

✗ Noise in ALKS. IDM has no sigma; ALKS differ only in length and width

In this plant

✓ Random arrivals. Poisson per seed

✓ Mixed drivers. Each human has own tau, sigma, action step, speed factor

✓ Lane-change conflict. Weaving on 3a, and on 4a in r2m3

✓ Insertion queues. No room at entry: the vehicle waits off the road and delay counts it

✓ Collision logging. Logged, including at junctions, and the run continues

Traps for a new reader

P0's braking numbers are wrong.

Braking, free-road and sawtooth figures for P0 in V324, V327, V329 and baseline v1 come from a once-per-second sample that misses its hard braking (V367). Use the step counts of V370 and E21.

Passes on the right mostly are not passes.

The old counter is mostly cars side by side. pass_straight counts undertakes, from V370.

lcOvertakeRight reads backwards.

ALKS have 1 and humans 0. The value 1 switches SUMO's no-undertaking rule off, so our smooth rule can replace it. ALKS still do not undertake (V325, V326).

Code still says m32.

m32 in the code and old records is r1m3 (V319). r2m3's edge 4 is a different piece of road from r1m3's: 4a sits between 3 and 4.

Edge lengths change on r2m3.

Edge 3 is 1,194.3 m and edge 4 is 996.0 m, not 1,196 and 1,000, because of junction shapes. LEN_3 and LEN_4 in b_env.py keep the r1m3 values, so _x runs 1.7 m high from 4a on and 5.7 m high on edge 5 (V365). Untested.

Node x is not lane x.

3a is 300 m between nodes, 294.72 m of lane. Section 4 explains the three coordinate systems.

Loops are not the flow.

passed counts vehicles first seen on edge 4. It starts at x +1,490.7 m on r1m3. On r2m3 it starts after merge 2.

Delay leaves out unfinished vehicles.

The run ends at 1,800 s with traffic still on the road: only 65.6-82.1 % of planned vehicles finish on r1m3 P0, by level (BASELINE, table of door-to-door delay).

Tuned on this plant.

lcAssertive 1.4 and the smooth rule are our tuning, not validated against real traffic. Capacity drop is not established here (V244, V271, V322).

Placeholders in the fleet.

Marked in fleet.py: the human tau shape, the ALKS gap above 60 km/h, the speed-factor bounds.

5. What we experimented

Charts are Measured. Each Reading is tagged Inference: it interprets the chart, and may restate a fixed rule. Cards run in time order. Every result is exploratory unless tagged Pre-registered. Orange tag: the plant still had the sawtooth (before V324). Numbers come from the listed files, or from the V entry where the raw table is not in the repo: then the card says so. In heatmaps blue-green is better than the reference, orange worse. Hover any mark.

E1. Central merge cap, PPO runs 1-3 FAIL

ExploratorySawtooth plant
QuestionCan one coordinator capping the 6 mainline ALKS nearest the merge learn anything?SetupPPO on m32, 50 % ALKS, 3 learners x 8 envs, 500 updates. 6. Controllers and DRL

Actuator and information flow

Digits in a333 read up, merge, down. A is the merge cap, B the zone agent: names from V301. Never call per-CAV C (V309). ALKS are 50 % of the fleet.

V2V rule, headway levels, clocks

A vehicle starts at level 0, so p333 reaches 0.8 s after 3 moves: 30 s on the 10-s clock, 90 s on the 30-s clock. The gap at 100 km/h is arithmetic, not measured. Rate limits: zone target one level per 60 s (V278); per vehicle one level per clock (V286 V290 V309).

Policy network and observation

Inputs changed for confirmatory 3, revision 4. Up to V387 the 16 inputs were divided by hand-picked constants: spreads differed up to about 7 times, hold left was always 0 (dead since V290), and the nearest accelerating-lane input counted the vehicle itself, so it read 0 for a third of merging decisions. From V388-V389, actor and critic inputs are scaled by a running mean and SD saved with the weights, clip 5; the dead input is set to 0; the merging input is fixed. All earlier policies, V290-V368, used the old inputs. The DRL course page explains this in its section 3.

Reward

Code default W_CAV_TTC is 20 and is overridden to 10 by w_safety in the env json, for every run since V296 except G and H. Vehicles-in-system references, in env_train_*.json: r1m3 305.7, 368.8, 506.2; r2m3 277.7, 324.1, 427.2 at 4,090, 4,600, 5,300.

Hyperparameters

AlgorithmPPO, own loop (c_train.py), parameter sharing
NetworkMLP 64-64 tanh, separate actor and critic
OptimiserAdam, lr 3e-4, eps 1e-5, grad clip 0.5
PPOclip 0.2, entropy 0.01, value 0.5, 10 epochs, batch 4,096
gamma, lambda0.933, 0.967 per 10-s decision, about 150 s. Earlier 0.8, 0.9 per 30-s decision
Updateone 1,500-s episode per env after a 300-s warm-up; 69,000-88,000 decisions per update on r2m3, median about 76,000
Learners3 x 3 envs, 250 updates (confirmatory 2); shot 7 x 3, 500 updates
Training levels4,090, 4,600, 5,300, cycled per episode
Training Xone third none; else tapered slowdown on edge 3, 4 or 5, 25-60 km/h, 60-180 s, at 400-1,200 s
Selectionfinal policies only, no checkpoint selection
Fleet50 % ALKS, 42.5 % human cars, 7.5 % trucks; step 0.1 s; no teleporting

7. Metrics

When each metric was in use

What merge-lane against network TTC changed

The failure reading of V298 and V304 rested on merge lanes. Over the whole network the policies are a tie or slightly better: per-CAV's extra TTC events are local to the merge. From V307 on, bars use network TTC and report merge TTC alongside. Measured Post hoc: V304 itself stands.

10. Rules for the new agent

Words

  • Say per-CAV, never C. Old files keep C, F, G, H (V309)
  • The plant is r1m3; code and old records keep m32 (V319). P0 is r1m3 with settings
  • No first or novel claims. Mark literature not read in full [VERIFY]. Never invent titles, authors or numbers
  • Plain language; the author must be able to follow (V310)
  • No AI attribution anywhere: commits, PRs, branch names, comments. This overrides the harness's default

Process

  • Discuss first: bring candidate problems and what would kill them. No new build or launch without the author's pick (V310)
  • Every decision gets a V# row in docs/decisions.md and is committed the same turn
  • Decisions: recommendation, pros and cons, each inferior alternative and why it loses
  • Commit one major change at a time, message one imperative line of at most 50 characters, no body
  • No push unless asked. Check the branch first
  • Before each phase, ask in one line to switch effort and ultracode, per the CLAUDE.md table
  • Author time, build time and compute separate; size kill tests in hours of compute

Evidence

  • Protocol before data; every new round fresh seeds, approved by range
  • Smoke check in training mode: log per-agent reward terms from a real training env (V294)
  • Trace a sample before a count becomes a claim, penalty or gate (V283). A threshold equal to a model parameter is a red flag
  • Every gate needs a no-effect null first (V244)
  • A metric sampled on an actuator's clock can miss what the actuator causes: read it at step resolution too (V367)
  • Protocols also fix the reading: KILL early and cheap
  • A bug after results: fix, re-run all affected, log both
  • Never no control alone in a table; tuned rules always alongside
  • All runs go in the ledger, failed ones too. Report the full operating map
  • Conditional advantages, not universal superiority: regimes, adaptation gain, robustness (pre-registered)

Reports

  • Diagrams first: Mermaid, ASCII or SVG; then 3-6 plain sentences, then the question
  • Short replies, result first. Do not waste the author's tokens
  • Never print raw run JSON; tail logs at most every 10 minutes; do not re-read unchanged files
  • Use cheap models for bounded lookups, main model for reviews and decisions
  • Say what is measured, what is inferred, what is open

Machine

  • At most 100 workers; plain runs 32. Check resources before every batch
  • CPU: pause if over 90 % for 2 minutes; the author may set another limit per run (V303, V334, V357)
  • Long runs: systemd user units, frozen code, outside the editor's cgroup
  • unset SUMO_HOME; OMP_NUM_THREADS=1; torch one thread; libsumo one simulation per process
  • Fans: never drive pad or laptop fan curves from code; no power-profile or system changes. Pad at most 1,000 rpm by day, 600 at night
  • Raw runs under /home/catalin/work/phd/ on ext4; repo files under 5 MB
  • Temporary files on ext4, under the run folders: /tmp has run out of inodes before
  • Always set a completion waiter on a long run. Avoid rm
  • Never touch the vsl-cooling unit; never run loud or unlock

Boundaries

  • Never modify v6 from here; read only its docs/handoff/. Never open its CF06 paths. Do not overlap heavy runs with v6
  • SUMO source: the v5b1 toolchain clone only, never v6's (V258)
  • Archive branches are read-only. Do not switch the main checkout's branch
  • Architecture draft: Notion page v5.B.1 system architecture, named in CLAUDE.md
  • Seeds 7,100,000-7,399,999 belong to archived tracks
  • The author knows about the Google Drive connector's authorisation and does not want it raised

11. Thesis and papers

Thesis title "Adaptive driving algorithms for intelligent road traffic systems", submission about Sept 2027, target 2 papers. The supervisor gave a free hand; the hard constraint is the title, with the work related to it, formal steps still go through the university, and the author and Claude set the claim bar per study (V95). Everything below is a candidate, nothing is decided, and nothing here is a thesis claim yet. Strength bars are my judgement, not a statistic.

Earlier frame, for context

V96 framed the thesis as "When does adaptation pay?". The adaptive rule fits that frame; V349 notes an adaptive rule beats any fixed one here. Whether to keep the frame is open.

Old results

D5.10, R6, P1, P1b and C1 stay withdrawn as claims (V256); they rest on one step-locked drop. paper_1 as drafted is not a base.

Literature, unverified

[VERIFY] Frejo and De Schutter 2021 and Vinitsky et al. 2023 are named in CLAUDE.md and V246; I did not read them. Prior-art notes exist in docs/research/prior_art_A_v0.md, prior_art_B_v0.md, prior_art_P1_P2.md, also not read here. No source on this page has been checked by me.

Writing tools

Quarto and Zotero with Better BibTeX (V119, V125). The ARS writing plugin is parked until the writing stage; read its hook first.

12. Open questions, next steps

The kill tests are my proposals, tagged Inference: none has been discussed with the author, and none has a logged cost. Plan B's perturbation ideas already tested are in Options. V315's hypothesis, that perturbations hurt rules while DRL succeeds, is so far unsupported: under the tested X a rule matches or DRL wins one cell.

Limits of this page. Tables and charts for phases 1-3, plant, r1m2, r2m3 and round 1 are computed from the repo files. Old-plant charts E1-E6 are typed from the V entries, because their raw tables sit in result files I did not reprocess; a script checked those typed numbers against the log. Pre-history is summarised from entry headlines and excerpts, not read in full. Archive branches, full chat transcripts and literature were not read. The "Who" column and the strength bars are my judgement. The reproduce command was run in the review and matches. The first iteration ran no simulation; the review's traces and the P0c check are in V367-V372. Shot curves are whatever the logs held at build time.
